title: Bears Rookie Gets Thrown Into the Fire in Week 1
description: Dillon Thieneman dreamed about his first NFL regular-season game as a kid. Now, the Chicago Bears rookie safety will get […]
fullText:
Dillon Thieneman dreamed about his first NFL regular-season game as a kid. Now, the Chicago Bears rookie safety will get there with far more on his shoulders than most first-year players could expect.

The Bears open their 2026 season Sunday against the Carolina Panthers needing Thieneman to be more than a promising young player. They need him to be steady. They need him to communicate. And, most of all, they need him to help eliminate the backbreaking explosive plays that undermined their defense in recent years.

That is a massive assignment for any rookie, particularly one walking into an unsettled safety room.

Chicago lost projected starter Coby Bryant to a major knee injury during training camp, and the team placed slot cornerback Kyler Gordon on the physically unable-to-perform list. Gordon must miss at least the first four games, potentially more. The Bears have veteran options in Xavier Woods and Cam Lewis alongside Thieneman, but neither uncertainty disappears simply because the regular season is here.

Thieneman, the rookie selected 25th overall in April, has become the constant.

That is not how the Bears envisioned their back end at the start of camp. But Thieneman handled the summer well enough that the team can reasonably expect him to play a major role immediately. His range, instinctiveness and willingness to tackle have shown up throughout camp and the preseason. His next challenge is preventing the mistakes that turn a good defensive call into a 40-yard gain.

Dillon Thieneman showing off the range to breakup this pass intended for Carnell Tate

Future perennial Pro Bowler pic.twitter.com/AFQ6eJrwaJ

Chicago's defense struggled to limit explosive plays last season, a weakness that puts more pressure on its reshaped safety group. That is not a problem one player can solve alone, but safeties are often the final line of defense when a coverage breaks down or a runner gets through the first two levels.

Thieneman knows the difference between merely understanding the system and playing quickly within it.

"I've got a better understanding of tendencies," he said Monday. "So now it's taking that next step and not only just knowing it, but being able to anticipate it and use it to your advantage."

That is the leap the Bears need him to make sooner rather than later.

Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's scheme should help. Thieneman said the defense has structure and rules, but Allen does not want defenders frozen by the call sheet. He gives players room to communicate, adjust and trust what they see before the snap.

"I think it's pretty simple," Thieneman said. "Obviously, there's complexities within it, but a lot of times he makes a call and he lets people on the field just play football. … If we see it a little differently, he's like, 'You guys are out on the field. You guys call it.' That's been pretty cool."

That freedom is valuable, but it also demands maturity. A rookie safety can get himself into trouble by trying to make the perfect play rather than the correct one. Thieneman will have to balance his aggressive instincts with the discipline to stay on top of routes, make the proper checks and ensure everyone in the secondary sees the formation the same way.

The Bears did not leave him alone to figure that out. Thieneman has spent camp working alongside Lewis and Woods, two veterans with far more NFL experience. He said he feels comfortable with both players and regularly talks through what they saw on the field and the sideline.

"They definitely have a lot of experience able to help me," Thieneman said. "I've been talking to them a lot just in the meeting room, like how they see things. And out on the field, we'll talk once we're on the sideline. But I feel very comfortable and able to communicate and kind of anticipate what the other guys are thinking."

That comfort matters because Chicago could need all three players in different roles. Lewis has experience at safety and nickel cornerback. Woods brings physicality and has pushed for a starting job since signing late in camp. Rookie Malik Muhammad appears positioned to begin in the slot while Gordon is sidelined, but the Bears have options if they decide they need Lewis there instead.

The lineup may change. Thieneman's importance will not.

He has already received practical advice on handling the inevitable ups and downs of a rookie season. Assistant defensive backs coach Matt Giordano told him to learn from the bad moments without letting them linger.

"Just take it one day at a time," Thieneman said. "Something bad happens, learn from it, move on. Don't linger too long."

That philosophy will get tested quickly. The Panthers will look for every communication lapse and every inexperienced defender they can isolate. The Bears cannot bet on their rookie safety to be perfect in Week 1, but they need him to be poised.

Thieneman has waited a long time for this moment. The Bears are asking him to make the most of it immediately.

title: Jemele Hill goes off at Shaquille O’Neal’s ‘false narrative’ amid Stephen A. Smith and Cari Champion fiasco
description: Shaquille O’Neal receives a brutal response from Jemele Hill over Stephen A. Smith’s defense.
fullText:
Shaquille O'Neal receives a brutal response from Jemele Hill over Stephen A. Smith's defense.

NBA analyst Stephen A. Smith, Jemele Hill, and Cari Champion continue to make headlines after the ESPN icon's alleged three-hour interview with them.

Smith has alleged that Hill and Champion edited clips out of the interview to make him look bad rather than clearing the air about his 2014 comments.

Now, NBA legend Shaquille O'Neal has joined the conversation, but the former LA Lakers superstar received a brutal response from Hill.

All O'Neal did was repost Smith's demand that Hill and Champion release the full footage of the interview. But Hill interpreted it as feeding into the false narrative.

As a result, Hill posted a lengthy response to the Diesel on X, stating, "I hate to even address this because it's feeding a false narrative.

"The full interview is out on iHeart, Apple Podcasts, or wherever you get your podcasts and has been that way from the beginning. An editing mistake occurred involving the video, and no, Cari and I don't have anything to do with the video, and that is why there is some video footage unaccounted for."

Hill added, "This mistake was shared with Stephen A's team, and they were also provided a full transcript as well as told exactly how it happened. Nothing nefarious occurred.

"Trust me, there is no smoking gun in the unseen video footage, and you can go to the audio and listen for yourselves. The 20 minutes that is alleged to be missing is all there in the audio version."

Hill blamed the mistake on the editing team as she put Smith's claims to bed. But will it be enough to calm the ESPN analyst and, more importantly, Shaq? Only time will tell.

title: Wycombe sack boss Duff after winless start
description: Wycombe Wanderers sack Michael Duff and his assistant Alex Morris just five games into the League One season.
fullText:
Wycombe Wanderers have sacked Michael Duff as manager following a five-game winless start to the new League One season.

First-team coach Alex Morris has also left the club in the wake of the Buckinghamshire side having picked up just three points out of a possible 15.

The 48-year-old former Cheltenham Town, Barnsley, Swansea City and Huddersfield boss had been in charge almost a year after replacing Michael Dodds on 18 September 2025, having made a similarly poor start to last season.

Wycombe recovered to finish in the top half of the table and although they have only actually lost twice this time round in the league, it has not stopped Duff becoming the first managerial casualty of the campaign in the top four divisions.

"The appointment of an interim head coach will follow later today," said a club statement.

"The club has made the decision in light of a disappointing run of results since the spring and believes the time is right to take a new direction."

Although they beat Rotherham on the final day of last season, that has been Wycombe's sole victory in their past 13 games, in all competitions, including this season's Carabao Cup defeat by Stevenage and the Vertu Trophy draw at Reading.

Former Crewe Alexandra manager Morris had been with Wycombe since October 2025, after spending two years on the coaching staff at Stoke City.

title: Haste ye back to full health, gaffer
description: This column is usually filled with bad takes, daft footballing opinion and poor attempts at humour, but today I want to be a little more serious.  The gaffer, Jim Goodwin, is going through a health issue at present.  As a player, Goodwin was never my favourite, in fact, he likely wasn't anyone's favourite.
fullText:
This column is usually filled with bad takes, daft footballing opinion and poor attempts at humour, but today I want to be a little more serious.

The gaffer, Jim Goodwin, is going through a health issue at present. And for his own and his family's sake, I hope he can return to full health as soon as possible.

As a player, Goodwin was never my favourite, in fact, he likely wasn't anyone's favourite. For a start, he was always in the opposition, but I'll concede, he played the game in an honest and often robust manner.

He'd tell you himself he wasn't the best player to pull on a pair of boots, but he made the most of 'what he had'. That in itself is admirable.

Since becoming Dundee United manager, it's been clear to see he's a passionate, amiable, well-spoken, determined, thoughtful and proud man, who has represented our club wonderfully well and given his absolute all.

Through no fault of his own, he's had to build four teams in his time at Tannadice. With those teams he has achieved, I would imagine, most of what was asked of him, albeit this season is still in its infancy.

He has fronted up every week, regardless of result, and taken the full force of flak and blame when there are also others at fault when things haven't gone well. Yes, I'm looking at you lot upstairs.

Far be it from me to speculate what Goodwin is going through, but he and every other manager in the league must experience some amount of stress on a near daily basis.

Yes, football managers are in a relatively privileged position, but we need to remember they are human. They have good days, they have difficult days. They also suffer from ill health at times, and when that happens, football tends to pale into insignificance.

So from myself and many, many others, I wish you well, Jim. Haste ye back to health and the dugout.

Paul McNicoll can be found at the Dode Fox Podcast

title: Week 1 Fantasy Football Injury Report: TreVeyon Henderson, George Kittle And More
description: The 2026 NFL season begins with Week 1 injury reports heavily influencing fantasy football decisions.
fullText:
At long last, the 2026 NFL season is about to begin. While there's still time to squeeze in a few final fantasy football drafts, managers are already having to parse injury reports as they make their lineup decisions for Week 1.

On Wednesday night, the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks will host the New England Patriots in a rematch of Super Bowl LX. The Patriots overhauled their receiving corps this offseason by adding AJ Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles and Romeo Doubs from the Green Bay Packers, but their skill-position corps could be down a key player against Seattle.

On Thursday, the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will clash in Melbourne, Australia, with plenty of injury question marks on both sides. Fantasy managers did get some clarity on Monday about one veteran receiver, but uncertainty otherwise still abounds in this matchup.

The season kicks off in full on Sunday with 13 games on the docket. Teams playing Sunday don't have to submit their first injury report until Wednesday, so we won't get updates on a pair of key running backs until then. But we're already starting to get a steady trickle of updates hinting at who may—and may not—be available for Week 1.

Every Tuesday, we'll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup for the upcoming week. Let's dive into all of the most notable updates ahead of Week 1.

New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson hasn't practiced since Aug. 24 because of an ankle injury, leaving his status for Week 1 up in the air. He missed practice Sunday and Monday, although the Patriots still haven't clarified his official status for Wednesday's season opener.

"We'll see how he feels today," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters prior to Monday's practice. "We'll see if he can do anything. He's been working extremely hard to come back, and we'll see where that goes here today. We do have a few more days before (the game), but we'll just see what he can do today."

According to ESPN's Mike Reiss, veteran tailback Rhamondre Stevenson would be the Patriots' starter even if Henderson does play, in part because the Patriots appear to trust him 

Fantasy managers with Henderson on their rosters should be exploring backup plans. Even if he does get declared active, is it worth the risk of him playing sparingly against a potentially stingy Seattle defense?

Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love suffered a high ankle sprain during his first preseason game on Aug. 13 and hasn't practiced since. Last week, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said he was "50/50" to play in the Cardinals' season opener against the Los Angeles Chargers.

However, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Monday that Love was "progressing" and "moving around" during the team's walkthrough. When asked about Love's chances of playing Sunday in the season opener, LaFleur replied, "I feel good."

Love piled up 11 carries for 58 yards and three catches for 14 yards against the Las Vegas Raiders in his lone preseason action, and he figures to be the focal point of the Cardinals' offense once he's back up to speed. It wouldn't be surprising if veteran tailback Tyler Allgeier siphoned off more work from Love in the red zone early on, though.

On Aug. 23, Vincent Bonsignore of the California Post briefly brought fantasy football managers to a halt when he reported Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty got hurt in practice and "could not put pressure on his leg when leaving the field." Thankfully, ESPN's Adam Schefter followed up later that night to add that Jeanty was "believed to have sprained his ankle" and it was "not considered a long-term injury."

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Jeanty's ankle sprain is "more low than high" and is "not considered to be a major injury." Last week, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters that he was optimistic about Jeanty being available for the season opener against the Miami Dolphins.

Backup running back Mike Washington Jr. dazzled during the preseason and is worth picking up in leagues of all sizes just in case Jeanty does miss time or aggravate his injury. But for now, it sounds like Jeanty managers dodged a major bullet even if he does wind up missing Week 1.

Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze exited practice last Thursday after he "came up hobbling during an install period," according to Sean Hammond of the Chicago Tribune. "He wasn't overly concerned—he tried to stay in—but trainers pulled him off," Hammond added.

Dan Wiederer of The Athletic reported "preliminary indications" were that Odunze "should be all good" after leaving practice. However, Odunze was absent from the Bears' practice on Monday, according to ESPN's Courtney Cronin.

The Bears might just be limiting Odunze's reps early in the week with an eye on getting him as close to 100% for the season opener. But until he's back on the practice field, managers should at least keep an eye on whether he'll be available against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. If not, wide receiver Luther Burden III and tight end Colston Loveland should be busy in the passing game.

San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle suffered a torn Achilles tendon during his team's Wild Card Round win over the Philadelphia Eagles in January. Eight months later, he might already be back on the field.

On Tuesday in Australia (Monday in the U.S.), Niners offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak told reporters that Kittle is "looking like himself, looking fresh." He added that Kittle is "practicing full speed" and is "getting a ton of reps" before hedging with, "How that affects on him on game day and what the workload is will be determined."

The Niners figure to ease Kittle back into action and not give him his typical complement of snaps in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams. Fantasy managers with Kittle on their rosters should at least considered having a backup plan in place even if he does play, as he could get eased back into action slowly.

Like Odunze, D'Andre Swift also left practice this past Thursday in "significant discomfort," according to Schefter. However, he was "said to be experiencing a 'cramp,'" Schefter added, and was back on the field at practice Monday. Cronin wrote in late August that Swift "had arguably the best training camp of any offensive skill player" for the Bears, so he should be wheels up for Week 1 against the Panthers.

Mike Evans missed time during training camp with quadricep and adductor injuries, but he told reporters in Australia that none of them "were significant." He added that had it been a normal game week, he "wouldn't have missed any time." Until Kittle is back up to speed, Evans has a chance to be the top red-zone target for quarterback Brock Purdy. He should be in fantasy lineups as long as he's healthy.

Puka Nacua dealt with a psoas injury in training camp, but Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay expects him to play Thursday against the Niners. Schefter also told ESPN's Pat McAfee that there's "a real possibility" Nacua doesn't face any discipline this season even though he's being sued for assault and battery by a woman "who says he made an antisemitic mark and bit her on the shoulder on New Year's Eve," according to the Associated Press. If he's playing, you're starting him. Simple as that.

Alec Pierce underwent ankle surgery in March and just returned to practice for the first time on Aug. 27, but Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen told reporters Monday that Pierce is expected to suit up Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is on the mend from a torn Achilles, so it wouldn't be surprising if the offense—and Pierce in particular—got off to a slow start. He'd be a risky play in Week 1, but he has far higher upside than most of the players being drafted in his range.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: The real reason Falcons chose Tua Tagovailoa over No. 8 pick Penix Jr.
description: The Falcons bench Michael Penix Jr. for Week 1. See why Kevin Stefanski chose Tua Tagovailoa and what this means for the season opener.
fullText:
The Atlanta Falcons made their choice clear before the season even kicked off. Head coach Kevin Stefanski named Tua Tagovailoa the starter for Sunday's opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers. That decision leaves Michael Penix Jr. on the sideline as an inactive player for the first game of 2026. It is a bold move for a team that spent the No. 8 overall pick on Penix in 2024. The organization also signed Kirk Cousins to a four-year deal that same offseason, showing they wanted a veteran path. Now, with Cousins gone and Penix hurt, the team turned to the former Miami Dolphins quarterback.

Tagovailoa signed a one-year deal with Atlanta back in March after Miami released him. His last season with the Dolphins was a mixed bag. He threw for 2,660 yards and 20 touchdowns, but he also tossed a career-high 15 interceptions across 14 games. Those numbers matter because the Steelers have a tough defense waiting for them in Pittsburgh. Stefanski did not hide his reasoning. He said the evaluation was "all-encompassing" and looked at everything Tagovailoa has done since April.

Penix was cleared for full 11-on-11 work on August 22, yet he will not dress for the game. This creates a weird situation where a player is medically cleared but still not ready for the field. Stefanski explained that medical clearance is different from game readiness. "You can get cleared for 11-on-11 or you get cleared for a game, but then you have to be able to do your job," Stefanski explained. The coach compared it to offensive tackles who might be healthy enough to play but cannot function at the needed level.

Yahoo Sports Canada reports Penix began nine games with the Falcons in 2025 prior to an ACL tear in November. He has a 4-8 record as an NFL starter. The team wants him back, but not at the cost of a loss in Week 1. The Falcons chose to protect their investment rather than rush him back. This means Cooper Rush will serve as the backup quarterback.

Tagovailoa knows the system better than anyone else on the roster right now. He started the first and last of Atlanta's preseason games. In the third preseason game against Miami, he went 7 of 8 for 95 yards, per Yahoo Sports Canada. He led a 60-yard touchdown drive on the opening possession, though he did lose a fumble on the next one. Stefanski praised the work Tagovailoa put in during camp. "But I've gotten to see (Tagovailoa) work really, really hard throughout this entire process of learning a new system, learning his teammates," Stefanski said.

Knowledge of teammates is huge for a quarterback. "So much of quarterback play comes down to knowing your teammates," Stefanski said. "You've got to know how this receiver comes out of this break versus that receiver," he added. Despite the praise, the job is not safe. Stefanski noted that if Tua is named the starter early this week, it will be on a little bit of a short leash based on the health of Michael Penix Jr. Penix is getting closer to returning, but he is still not 100% just yet. The Falcons hope this gamble pays off, but the pressure is on immediately.

title: Blue Jays Nation Challenges ‘Petulant Child’ Donald Trump After Lake America Update
description: The Toronto Blue Jays were at the center of political debate after U.S. President Donald Trump renamed Lake Ontario amid a trade dispute.
fullText:
The Toronto Blue Jays spent one of their final series of the regular season turning a road stadium into something resembling home games, with fans traveling across the border to support a team fighting for an American League playoff spot.

During Toronto's recent series against the Cleveland Guardians, a matchup that carried major wild-card implications, Blue Jays fans traveled en masse. The Blue Jays won the season series and, in the process, secured an important tiebreaker that could become critical if the teams finish with identical records.

"The Blue Jays hold the tiebreaker over the Guardians after winning the season series earlier this week," Sportsnet noted on Monday. "Both teams have 18 games remaining."

But the Toronto-Cleveland series also carried some political weight as the teams' respective nations engage in a tense trade war with significant rhetorical implications.

Dodgers' Pending $400 Million Free Agent Could 'Gravitate' Toward Angels Contract

The recent Guardians series provided a striking reminder of how many Blue Jays supporters cross the U.S.-Canada border to follow their team.

"If you closed your eyes, you might have thought the Blue Jays were playing at home," Mike Wilner reported for the Toronto Star. "Over a three-game series with huge playoff implications, every Jays' run was met with loud cheers and there were several spontaneous chants of 'Let's go Blue Jays!' that rained down from the seats at Progressive Field in Cleveland, which sits at the corner of Ontario Street and Carnegie Avenue."

That cross-border connection took on a different dimension after President Donald Trump issued an executive order directing the federal government to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America."

The White House order, signed August 27, directs the Interior Department and Board on Geographic Names to take steps to rename the body of water and update the federal Geographic Names Information System. The order describes the lake as an important American economic and strategic asset.

The decision has drawn attention in Canada, particularly because Lake Ontario is shared by the United States and Canada. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has continued referring to the body of water as Lake Ontario.

And for several Blue Jays fan attending the Cleveland series, the political dispute couldn't be ignored.

Joshua Glass, travelling with a friend who gracefully exited the conversation when he heard what the topic was going to be, doesn't share his fellow fans' hesitance.

"I'm not going to pay attention to the rantings of a petulant child, quite frankly," said Joshua Glass, one Blue Jays fan in attendance in Cleveland, according to Wilner. "It's not going to keep me from going to see my team fight for a wild-card spot. I think the whole thing is a bit ridiculous, but it's not going to prevent me from coming ... I'm going to be here no matter what. Until they close the border, that is."

While the political dispute didn't seem to turn Blue Jays away from supporting their favorite team in Cleveland, several of them indicated that Trump's latest geographic moniker decision did give them second thoughts about visiting the U.S.

"After the whole 'Lake America'/Lake Ontario thing," a fan named Melissa told Wilner. "You kind of get numb to the whole 'We're going to charge you tariffs' and everything like that, but as it just escalates now you just kind of get turned off from wanting to come, but I'm going to love the game."

Member Of Yankees' Legendary World Series Championship Roster Dies

For the Blue Jays, the larger story remains the playoff race. Toronto and Cleveland were separated by the thinnest of margins entering the final stretch, making their season series particularly significant.

And the passionate Cleveland turnout demonstrated that Toronto's fan base remains willing to travel when the stakes rise. With the Blue Jays pursuing a wild-card berth, that support could continue to follow them throughout the postseason chase.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Donald Trump could have surprising role at Irish Open this weekend as Rory McIlroy stars in home event

fullText:

The event is being held at the stunning Trump International Golf Links & Hotel in Doonbeg, on Ireland's west coast.

It is the first time that Donald Trump's course will host the Irish Open, and the president does not want to miss out.

Rory McIlroy raised the profile of the Irish Open with his sensational playoff victory over Joakim Lagergren 12 months ago.

Thousands of fans are expected to attend this year's event, with big names such as McIlroy, Jon Rahm, and Shane Lowry in the field.

However, Donald Trump is likely to steal much of the spotlight when he flies to Ireland this weekend.

Trump is set to arrive on Saturday for a meeting with Irish President Catherine Connolly and Prime Minister Micheal Martin.

However, the BBC has reported that Trump will attend the Irish Open and could even stay for the trophy presentation.

Therefore, we could see the United States president on the 18th green at Doonbeg on Sunday.

title: Filipe Luís confirms Monaco’s continued Erik Lira pursuit
description: AS Monaco manager Filipe Luís has said that he will “continue to want Erik Lira in every transfer window”. It comes after the Principality club missed out on the Mexico international this summer....
fullText:
AS Monaco manager Filipe Luís has said that he will "continue to want Erik Lira in every transfer window". It comes after the Principality club missed out on the Mexico international this summer.

Lira was a target for the Principality club throughout the summer. However, his arrival was always blocked due to there being no non-EU spots in the squad. The expected departure of Folarin Balogun was expected to free one up, however, his move to Everton was not completed.

Speaking at Wednesday's press conference, attended by Get French Football News, Monaco's CEO, Thiago Scuro, confirmed the talks. "The situation with Erik Lira, our relationship with Cruz Azul… I want to really thank them, and I appreciate the way they dealt with everything with us. The deal was ready. The player was ready to travel. Everything was absolutely pressing on the button. But it was mandatory in the agreement that Balogun would open the foreign (Non-EU) spot; because of that, we were not able to bring Erik Lira. That was our desire. Having to call the player and say, I'm sorry, we couldn't make it. As a human, it's a very hard part of the job during the transfer window," he said.

The Monaco CEO was then asked about renewing their pursuit in January. "It depends on several things. We are not in a position to ask them to wait, keep holding. But for sure, it's a player that has our attention and respect," added Scuro. With Luís also still very keen on recruiting the midfielder, a future transfer is a possibility.

title: Football-tangential things to look forward to during the 2026 NFL regular season
description: These are the things I love about football, beyond the actual football
fullText:
You're likely not reading this if you don't think football is awesome. The most casual of observers don't come to SB Nation sites and click on stories to read on a random weekday. Thus, I'm not telling you anything you don't already know. But it's not just the actual sport of football, played between whistles, that makes us love football so much. It's all the phenomena that are football-related that add to our enjoyment of the season that always seemed too short.

First, I would encourage you to share the non-football events, moments, or traditions that make the sport's 18+ weeks so much fun for you in the comments below (maybe someone can pick up an enjoyable idea). Secondly, I'll share some of mine here:

I strongly ascribe to the belief that traditional food calendars should not influence your culinary choices. If you want stew on a hot summer day, you should have it. If it's the dead of winter and you want some ice cream, get some ice cream. Whether it's a usually-prepared "summer food" or not should not stop you from enjoying it. When it's considered seasonally appropriate, who knows if it'll hit the spot then? I will not be oppressed by the tyranny of the fictitious food calendar!

That being said, certain people and restaurants do not ascribe to my progressive culinary thinking. Because of that, my food options are sometimes slightly limited by what the person or establishment deems appropriate for the season, and that exclusion stops now. If I was a pumpkin spice person like my wife (to complete the ensemble with the Ugg boots and leggings), I'd be blocked off from getting it until the Starbucks overlords deemed appropriate to bless the peasants with that overly-nutmegged (that's totally a word) liquid concoction. So I'm excited for the new wing flavors. I'm excited for all the caramel apple desserts. I'm excited for my local shop to start offering their pumpkin rolls again.

As long as I'm forced to live in a society that doesn't let me have the easiest access to apple fritters in June, I'll be grateful for the return of some elite-tier foods.

Much like my above take on food, I'm a "wear what you want, when you want"-kind of guy…

…but you know, the weather and stuff.

As long as you live in the Northern Hemisphere, fall and winter are cooler than summer. How much cooler depends on your location, but for a lot of people, American football season (and the immediate aftermath) is the only time they can wear a hooded sweatshirt outside their house without it quickly serving as an inadvertent sauna suit. The joy of this article of clothing is also related to the first point identified above, as the magic of the hoodie allows for a few extra fall pounds to be packed onto a human body secretly, well hidden by the sweatshirt until which time as the spring comes and we begin to slightly regret our football-related consumption choices.

Maybe the Bills should play Josh Allen at linebacker.

Maybe Aaron Kromer should have been made the head coach.

Win or lose, the people who call into stations like WGR 550 or 97 Rock (the new Buffalo Bills flagship station) immediately post-game can provide some of the most unhinged and galaxy-brained ideas and takes that anyone sober could ever truly appreciate. No matter what you believe to be the most relevant issues surrounding the team after a regular season or playoff game, the hard left and right turns provided to you by some of the individuals who call into the post-game radio shows make the programs must-listen simply for the entertainment value of their takes alone, completely apart from the competence of the radio hosts themselves.

I don't typically go to Bills games. I went to the first football game ever played in the new Highmark Stadium when Buffalo took on the Carolina Panthers in the preseason, but I hadn't been in years prior to that and likely won't go again for a while.

But even I love the adventures that can only come from Bills tailgating. Throwing the football with strangers who become friends over some grilled food, irresponsibly jumping into tables, spraying ketchup and mustard all over yourself (for some reason I still haven't quite figured out)…it all makes for adventures and stories that people can tell each other for years to come. It's part of the quintessential Buffalo football experience. Other sports try it, other teams try it, but there's something special about it specifically for members of Bills Mafia. I smile every time the TV feed shows people who have obviously been tailgating for hours or ever days prior to the game, and I root for all y'all to have an excellent, yet safe, time.

Social media gameday traditions

Brother Bill (@TheeBrotherBill on Twitter) announced recently that his famous gameday morning opponent-specific videos (set to the tune of "Seven Nation Army" by the White Stripes) would be discontinued after seven years of providing laughs and coffee-beers to the member of Bills Mafia on social media, but other traditions remain. Greg Tompsett of Cover 1 (@GregTompsett) will still attempt to make the perfect steak the night before the game to "earn the right to win". His teammate Aaron Quinn (@AaronQuinn716) will still post his breakfast sandwiches. I will still type out the word "I hope the Bills win today" and post it every game day (I'll chuckle when I do it).

Traditions, even the tiniest ones, help create a shared community. And for Bills fans all over the globe who can't be physically in each other's presence like the tailgaters mentioned above, social media and websites like Buffalo Rumblings can help provide a venue for that community.

I love that football is back. But I love all the other little things that come alongside our beloved sport.

Let's do all of it together once again.

…and that's the way the cookie crumbles. I'm Bruce Nolan with Buffalo Rumblings. You can find me on Twitter and Instagram @BruceExclusive and look for new episodes of "The Bruce Exclusive" every Thursday on the Rumblings Cast Network — see

title: Bengals News: Getting Healthy
description: Game week comes with encouraging updates.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals were subject to a couple of injury scares in training camp, but they thankfully are getting healthy at the right time. As the first official game week rolls on, several impact players are back on the practice field.

Shemar Stewart was feared to have a serious knee injury just a few short weeks ago and now, it appears he could have a chance to play Week 1. As the revamped Bengals' defensive line looks to create havoc, Stewart meeting his potential could be crucial in getting the team back to the postseason.

Star wideouts Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins we're a bit banged up as training camp came to a close, but Monday's practice drew plenty of optimism for Sunday.

"The Bengals didn't show concern about wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins missing Week 1 when they missed practice last week and the outlook continues to be good as they move closer to Week 1."

"These guys are full of knowledge," Stewart told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "They know what they're talking about. They know how to set people up, they know how to track people. Even though I haven't been around playing football, I feel more situationally aware just hearing them talk in the meetings."

The Bengals have some familiar faces on their list of captains for 2026, but Dexter Lawrence II started earning the "C" on his chest immediately after the blockbuster trade in April. Now, he is the leader of the most important unit in 2026.

"I try to be genuine with everybody in this locker room because I care about them, and I care about this team, and I wanna win, it just happens naturally," Lawrence said. "I think you just take things from each one of those guys and implement it to yourself and keep growing, guys like Brian Burns is a great leader, Saquan is a great leader, you just pick and choose things that they do well good and try to implement it."

"Zac Taylor had a clear demand for fans, similar to what he asked of them last year, while he and the Bengals gear up for the 2026 opener."

title: Where can the Steelers rank top 10 in 2026?
description: The Steelers’ roster looks stronger than last year’s — could a top-10 finish on offense or defense be on the horizon?
fullText:
Top 10s have long been the standard of excellence when it comes to rankings, and in the 32-team NFL, it's a signifier of being in the top third of the league — not unachievable or elite, but above average in a game where even the smallest of margins can make a massive difference.

So, with the Steelers' regular season debut rapidly approaching this Sunday and predictions season starting to give way to actual football, let's take a look at where Pittsburgh could rank among NFL teams in the four main yardage metrics: passing, running, pass defense, and run defense. They're listed below based on how likely they are to land in the top 10 this season, from most to least.

Pittsburgh didn't finish as a top-10 team in any of these metrics in 2025. Could things change under a new coaching staff this year?

2025 finish: 13th in NFL; 113.1 rushing yards allowed per game

Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: This is a deep defensive line that features the ageless Cam Heyward and a bevy of run stuffers including Derrick Harmon, Yahya Black, Sebastian Joseph-Day and even impressive rookie Gabriel Rubio. Pittsburgh's edge rusher room is better defending the run than many realize as well. The strong front should open things up for an athletic inside linebacker room that could finally live up to its potential in Patrick Graham's aggressive scheme. And for the most part, the Steelers' secondary isn't afraid to tackle, with names such as DeShon Elliott, Jaquan Brisker and Jalen Ramsey all being known for laying out big hits in the box.

Why they won't: The range of the Steelers' inside linebacker room is not a question, but communication and block-shedding issues have been a common theme of past seasons for Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson. Top backup Cole Holcomb still doesn't look like the player he was pre-injury, either. The defensive line also isn't without its question marks. Heyward still looked elite last year but is now firmly in his late 30s. And a lot of the optimism surrounding the group's depth is banking on some sort of second-year leap from Harmon and Black, which isn't a guarantee.

2025 finish: 29th in NFL. 243.9 passing yards allowed per game.

Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: Pittsburgh boasts one of the deepest cornerback rooms in the NFL with an excellent projected starting trio in Joey Porter Jr., Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean (Killer J's, anyone?). Don't forget Jaquan Brisker, either, a versatile safety who should be a big improvement over the list of veterans the team cycled through last year. Pair that revamped secondary with a modern Patrick Graham scheme and star-studded pass rush, and the Steelers' passing defense has the pieces to take a big leap from its disappointing 2025.

Why they won't: Porter has barely practiced all summer and has hinted at a contract holdout. Ramsey will turn 32 this season. The starting secondary as a whole hasn't been the most available this summer and could still be gelling come Week 1. The safety depth chart could once again sink the defense, with a lack of range across the board and DeShon Elliott starting the season on injured reserve. There are a surprising number of factors that could go wrong.

2025 finish: 26th in NFL; 103.3 rushing yards per game

Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle are both 1,000-yard season-capable runners who give the Steelers one of the most underrated one-two punches in the NFL. The Zach Frazier/Mason McCormick duo should also be a powerhouse in the run game, and new head coach Mike McCarthy's more varied run scheme should give the team a more diverse ground attack that might better cater to some players' strengths. Keep in mind that tight end Darnell Washington might be the best run blocker at his position in the NFL, as well.

Why they won't: Warren and Dowdle are good but not superstars, and if the offensive line fails to generate enough push up front like what happened in the preseason, the team's running backs might not be able to create much yardage. Remember that the Steelers often needed to switch to a jumbo package or heavily use Washington last year to successfully run the ball, and the team will likely be using more 11 personnel in 2026. The right side of the Pittsburgh O-line doesn't have a ton of power, and the group as a whole was built for Arthur Smith's zone scheme, not a McCarthy system that uses more gap/power concepts.

2025: 22nd in NFL; 202.4 passing yards per game

Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: Aaron Rodgers' arm is still remarkably strong even at age 42, and the Steelers revamped the team's wide receiver room entering 2026 with the additions of veteran possession receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard. Despite a down 2025, WR1 DK Metcalf is still an explosive player and should see a boost in a modernized passing game under McCarthy. The same could be said of tight end Pat Freiermuth, who has been underused in past seasons but could finally break out under the coach who jumpstarted the careers of Jake Ferguson and Dalton Schultz. Don't underrate Warren's ability as a check-down target, either.

Why they won't: Rodgers had a historically fast time to throw last season, which shouldn't change much in 2026 considering the team is still catering to his preferences, the offensive line remains a work in progress, and Rodgers is still in his 40s and not going to be running around extending plays like he used to. That quick passing game could lead to a strong completion percentage, but it also doesn't do much to create big plays. And beyond Metcalf, the passing game is severely lacking in more options to gain chunk yardage.

Do you think the Steelers will rank in the top 10 in any of the above categories in 2026? What other metrics could Pittsburgh rank especially high or low in? Join the BTSC community and let us know in the comments.

title: New ‘Moment of Loudness’ tribute carries on important Utah tradition
description: For six consecutive years, the “Moment of Loudness” has become a closely-held tradition at Utah, one born out of tragedy.
fullText:
From the opening kickoff to the final whistle, Rice-Eccles Stadium is a cacophony of noise.

Some 51,444 fans are at full throat when the Utes score a touchdown or when the opposing defense is on the field. During the breaks in the three-plus-hour event, there's still noise at all times, from the marching band to music blasting from the speakers to the in-game presenter hyping fans up or announcing the contest.

There is one moment, aside from when the Utes are on offense, when Rice-Eccles Stadium falls relatively silent — during the break following the end of the third quarter.

For six consecutive years, the "Moment of Loudness" has become a closely-held tradition at Utah, one born out of tragedy.

In the span of just nine months, two University of Utah football players died. Ty Jordan, a freshman running back, died from an accidental shooting on Christmas night in 2020. Nine months later, sophomore cornerback Aaron Lowe, who was friends with Jordan and changed his number to Jordan's No. 22 for the upcoming season, was shot and killed at a party in September 2021.

It was an unimaginable loss for the players, staff and coaches within the Utah football program. Since the pair's tragic passing, Utah has honored them in a multitude of ways, from retiring the No. 22, setting up a "22 Forever" memorial scholarship, and honoring Jordan and Lowe with hand-painted helmets featuring their likeness that were worn in the Utes' memorable win over USC in 2022.

Each season, the program selects a recipient for the "22 Forever" scholarship that "exemplifies the inspiring qualities Ty and Aaron demonstrated." Lowe was actually the first recipient of the scholarship when it was in honor of just Jordan. Other recipients include JaQuinden Jackson, Money Parks, Smith Snowden and, this year, Alex Harrison.

𝘾𝙤𝙣𝙨𝙞𝙨𝙩𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙡𝙮 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙢𝙖𝙣 𝙣𝙚𝙭𝙩 𝙩𝙤 𝙝𝙞𝙢 🤝@BigAlHarrison1 couldn’t be more deserving of the 𝟮𝟮 𝗙𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗠𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗦𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗮𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽, as one who embodies the same qualities of his two former teammates 👏#GoUtes | #RSNB pic.twitter.com/48gdOK02Gc

The most visible of the ways Utah has honored Jordan and Lowe is the "Moment of Loudness," introduced Oct. 16, 2022, in a game against Arizona State. Instead of a moment of silence for the two players, Utah created a "moment of loudness" to celebrate their lives, accompanied by a video by Kyle Whittingham.

"Time and time again, you've heard of their smiles and how they could light up this stadium. Both Ty and Aaron exuded happiness and joy and they both defined what it meant to live, not just exist. To fight through hard times, to get back up when you fall, and to work to get 22% better every day. They left an impact on each of us and on you, our fans, that cannot be described," Whittingham narrated.

"So today, we ask — in honor of Ty and Aaron — that you smile. Smile big like they did. Smile, stand, cheer and let your voices ring from the mountains to the heavens in a moment of loudness, exuberance, joy and celebration for the lives of Aaron Lowe and Ty Jordan."

Over the years, the video has expanded to include fan-submitted photos of loved ones who have died and has become a celebration of the entire Utah football family — fans included.

With Whittingham gone, Utah made a new video for the "Moment of Loudness," which debuted in Saturday's win over Idaho. The new tribute featured narration from linebacker Devin Lloyd, cornerback Clark Phillips III, receiver Britain Covey, tight end Dalton Kincaid, cornerbacks coach Sharrieff Shah and head coach Morgan Scalley, each of whom played with or were on the coaching staff when Jordan and Lowe were at Utah.

Utah’s new Moment of Loudness pic.twitter.com/1CkJbrTpkL

Utah's new LED lighting system allowed the bright stadium lights to be lowered, with only a red glow illuminating the stadium. Rice-Eccles Stadium fell silent as the video began.

"This moment has become our tradition. A tradition that honors the lives of Ty Jordan and A Lowe. Being a Utah Man is bigger than one person, one game or one season. It's about being 22% better. Better for the guy next to you. Better for the guys who came before you and those who will come after you," the video shares.

"And with the tradition comes a commitment to be infectiously optimistic, to work hard, to get 22% more, and to be 22% better. To lift one another, to stand together. To carry forward the legacy of those who helped build this place, and to embrace each day with the same joy, purpose, and energy that Ty and Aaron shared with all of us.

"So with love in our hearts. We invite you to stand, smile and let your voices ring from the mountains to the heavens. This is Utah. This is family. This is our Moment of Loudness."

And with that, the crowd erupted as the submitted images of Utah fans that have passed on flashed on the screen.

College football isn't the highest level of the sport, but the reason it is so beloved by fans is because of the emotional connection they have to their teams. Oftentimes, you went to school there, or your parents did, passing down their love for the team to you.

Families spend time tailgating and attending games or watching on TV together, creating lifelong memories. Season-ticket holders that sit next to each other for years, and even decades, become friends.

In a sport rooted in tradition — fight songs, chants and marching bands — the Moment of Loudness is unique, evolving to provide fans the opportunity to reflect on their loved ones before celebrating them in a cathartic way and giving the players and coaches another chance to celebrate Jordan and Lowe.

Utah's creative team put together the latest video, and all of those players currently in the NFL came back to Rice-Eccles Stadium and the football facility to film it.

"For Clark, Dalton, and all those that were involved with that, they wanted to do that. So grateful for those guys. What a special moment just to keep that thing going," Scalley said.

"We just had, unfortunately, some tragedy in this program that has caused a lot of tears, but now it really allows for us to really celebrate the heck out of them."

The willingness of the players to do that illustrates the strong bond the program has with its players.

"This is something that happened in our program that really shook our program. And so that, in my opinion, it just shows how tight we are as a family," Scalley said. "The health of a college football program really, when you look at it, it's determined by, are your alumni giving back? Do your guys come back? Do they give to the program?

"And we've got an unbelievable group of former players that love this place, want to see it succeed. The amount of text messages that we all got today and yesterday about how fired up everyone was, it's really neat."

While talking about the Moment of Loudness in his postgame press conference, Scalley took the opportunity to remember Gaius Vaenuku, a freshman defensive tackle who was killed in a car accident in 2013 before Utah opened the season.

"I'll mention one other because I don't know that we talk about him enough. Gaius Vaenuku, not a lot of people remember Gaius. Gaius was one that never played for us, but he came out of Euless (Texas), Trinity (High). He was there the summer before his freshman year, traveling home to surprise his mom, got in a car accident, he passed away. That whole family, I continue to stay in contact with them," Scalley said.

For Utah, the Moment of Loudness continues to be a meaningful tradition and one that will continue well into the future.

"We just had, unfortunately, some tragedy in this program that has caused a lot of tears, but now it really allows for us to really celebrate the heck out of them," Scalley said.

title: Green Bay Roster: Breaking down the new Packers for 2026 and their roles
description: DL Javon Hargrave’s role with the Green Bay Packers is undefined going into the regular season
fullText:
As of now, the Green Bay Packers have 15 new players on their 53-man roster who weren't a part of the team in 2025. Today, we're going to break down every single one of these new players and what their expected roles on the team are, in case you missed any of the new from Green Bay this offseason.

There are also a couple of players I want to make a note of as honorable mentions, as they were technically members of the 2025 roster, but they didn't play in a single regular season game. Let's dive into who the new contributors will be for this year's team, starting off with the offensive skill players.

While he didn't have a good preseason, Tyrod Taylor threw 16 passes for 8 completions (50 percent) and just 38 yards (2.4 yards per attempt). The Packers never let anyone else take significant snaps with the second-team offense during training camp. After trading away Kyle McCord to the Miami Dolphins at the cutdown deadline, Green Bay's brass admitted that there was never really a competition for the job to back up Jordan Love, as Taylor was brought in to bring a veteran presence to the quarterback room.

With proven veteran backup quarterbacks generally going in the $5 million to $8 million range, the Packers got Taylor on the cheap, as he signed a one-year, $2.5 million deal with the team shortly after the 2026 NFL Draft. Taylor has previously played for Green Bay passing game coordinator Jason Vrable, who was the assistant quarterbacks coach with the Buffalo Bills in 2016, when Taylor was the starter there. Taylor is going into his 16th season in the NFL and has played in 100 games (62 starts, with a 29-31-1 record).

At the cutdown deadline, just before the news that starting running back Josh Jacobs was going to be put on the commissioner exempt list, the Packers traded for former Iowa and Pittsburgh Steeler running back Kaleb Johnson. Notably, Johnson played under Hawkeyes offensive coordinator Tim Lester, who served as a senior analyst for the Packers in 2023.

In 2025, Johnson was considered the 55th overall player in his draft class, according to the consensus draft board, but had some early struggles in Pittsburgh and fell down the depth chart. He's hoping to rebound with the Packers and their return to the outside zone scheme, which he ran frequently at the college level. He should back up MarShawn Lloyd as Green Bay's number two ball-carrying option (Chris Brooks is more of a blocking back) while Jacobs is out.

One of the few "compensatory free agents" that the Packers signed this spring was receiver Skyy Moore, who recently played for the San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Shanahan, a close friend of Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur. At the moment, it looks like Moore will be the backup slot receiver (behind Jayden Reed) offensively and also contribute as both a kick returner (at least until Savion Williams returns from his ankle injury) and as a punt returner.

The undrafted rookie streak lives on in Green Bay, and this year the man who kept it alive was former Florida (and Cal/UCLA) receiver J. Michael Sturdivant. Sturdivant should slide in behind Christian Watson as the backup Z receiver in the Packers offense while Savion Williams is sidelined, as they played similar roles (on both offense and special teams) during the summer.

Sturdivant also received reps on special teams as a gunner on the punt team, a lead blocker on the punt return team and as the "off returner" (a lead blocker role, unless he's kicked to) on the kickoff return unit. He was a lead blocker on kickoff return at the college level, too, so the 6'2.5", 207-pound receiver with 4.40-second speed is familiar with contributing on special teams.

To end the preseason, Sturdivant had his best performance of the summer, bringing in six receptions for 112 yards and a touchdown. That was the most yards a Packers receiver recorded in a single preseason game since 2011.

Head coach Matt LaFleur has a prior connection with Jonnu Smith, as he coached Smith when LaFleur was the offensive coordinator with the Tennessee Titans. Smith is famously an off-ball tight end who at times even carries the ball.

Don't go assuming Smith is an all-around tight end who is a threat when his hand is in the dirt. He's here to play a hybrid tight end-fullback role where he contributes to the offense by getting the ball in his hands.

Look for him to help out in obvious passing situations as a yards-after-catch threat. Eventually, whenever Luke Musgrave returns from the PUP list after his neck injury, Smith should push Josh Whyle out of his role on the team. At some point, the team will probably release Whyle, hoping to land him back on their practice squad, because they'll simply need roster numbers at another position.

We didn't get a look at Smith during the preseason, because he only officially signed with the Packers on the day of the cutdown deadline. When I've asked about why Green Bay didn't wait an extra day to sign Smith, I was told that the Packers had a practice that day and they wanted Smith to participate in it, the same reasoning for why long snapper Matt Orzech spent all of training camp on the PUP list but was activated on the day of cutdowns.

After the draft, general manager Brian Gutekunst stated that the team was disappointed that there wasn't value on the board for the Packers to take a true Y tight end, as there was a crazy run at the position starting in the second round of the draft. This void was eventually filled by Mark Redman, who was traded from the Los Angeles Rams at the cutdown deadline.

Worth noting: Redman was coached by Matt LaFleur's brother, Mike, when he was the offensive coordinator with the Rams in Redman's rookie season of 2025.

we have hoss potential with Rams TE #83 Mark Redman. pic.twitter.com/2XMOJjZUA7

There's a little uncertainty on the offensive line right now, because the team has been managing the recovery of left guard Aaron Banks (tendinitis) and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (partially torn patellar tendon) throughout the summer. With that being said, Banks' injury has given Jager Burton, a rookie fifth-round pick, a lot of opportunities to play with the first-team offense in both training camp and in the preseason.

If Banks can't go to start the year, assume that Burton will take over at left guard (because it seems like the starting right guard job has gone to Jacob Monk). Even if Banks is "starting," I'm not sure he won't be rotating with Burton, which has been a common occurrence for the 5th and 6th offensive linemen under Matt LaFleur's tenure as head coach.

Burton has really good traits and does some things well for a Day 3 rookie, but he also drops his head often when making blocks, which causes him some issues on stunts — particularly. He's green, but the faster he's onboarded, the better the Packers will be off long-term, in my opinion.

Because we didn't get an extended look at Javon Hargrave in the rotation during the preseason, the veteran defensive tackle's standing in the lineup is a bit of a question mark. There are signs that Karl Brooks is going to be the starting 3-4 defensive end opposite Devonte Wyatt, as Brooks has been pulled with the first-team defense around the same time as other established starters on defense, which leaves Hargrave's role on the team up in the air.

No matter who "starts," the interior defensive line unit should rotate significantly during the regular season, so everyone will get their opportunities. Maybe Hargrave, who played for defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon when the two were with the Philadelphia Eagles, will age into a pass-rushing specialist role. Keep an eye on this situation early on in the regular season.

The third-round rookie is probably right on the bubble of being a gameday active or not, depending on how many interior linemen the Packers feel like they can keep on the active 48. With Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Javon Hargrave primarily playing 3-4 defensive end and under tackle looks, Jonathan Ford being the team's true nose tackle and Warren Brinson being slightly ahead of Chris McClellan on the depth chart, he's probably the 6th priority at the defensive line position right now.

Will the Packers carry five or six players at the position? That's an open question right now. We tackled how carrying five interior linemen is one of the three reasonable options that Green Bay has for getting down to 48 players in our gameday roster projection.

With only four edge rushers currently on the Packers' 53-man roster, one rookie who will absolutely be playing for Green Bay to start the season is fourth-rounder Dani Dennis-Sutton. While he missed the first two preseason games of 2026 due to an overheating issue, Dennis-Sutton cleaned up against the Arizona Cardinals' reserves in the preseason finale. He looked every part of a freak designated pass-rusher in that game, even though he was mostly going against third-stringers.

Early on, I assume that Dennis-Sutton is going to be behind Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell and Brenton Cox Jr. in the pecking order, but look for Dennis-Sutton to get on the field in some obvious passing situations. He's very fun.

Near the start of the new league year, the Packers traded defensive lineman Colby Wooden to the Indianapolis Colts for linebacker Zaire Franklin. Franklin is now the team's green dot linebacker and starting Mike, while Wooden was waived by the team at the cutdown deadline and was picked up by the New Orleans Saints. Also, Franklin has already been named a team captain for Green Bay.

So far, the trade is looking like a big win for the Packers.

All of Brandon Cisse's pass coverage snaps through two preseason games. He's #2 always playing the (defense's) right cornerback pic.twitter.com/BGxg4qWBlN

With the way the Packers have been rotating at the cornerback position this summer, it's assumed that Keisean Nixon will be the team's starting left cornerback, but the right cornerback job will come down to incumbent starter Carrington Valentine and second-round rookie Brandon Cisse. As of now, the team has not officially named a starter at the position, but Cisse certainly built moment as training camp unfolded. Early on in camp, he was clearly third in the pecking order, followed by free agent signing Benjamin St-Juste.

I wouldn't be surprised if we see some sort of rotation between Cisse and Valentine at right cornerback to start the season, before one of them starts to run away with the job.

The Packers signed Benjamin St-Juste, who was the Los Angeles Chargers' fourth cornerback in 2025, to a modest contract that fits in line with some top special teams contributors at the position. His two-year deal really functions as a one year deal with a team option in 2027, so unless he ends up winning a starting job this year (unlikely), Green Bay will probably move on from him next year. Don't buy your St-Juste jersey just yet.

While Valentine and Cisse have been rotating at right cornerback, St-Juste has been playing left cornerback as Nixon's backup for most of training camp. As it stands right now, it would probably take an injury (or two) for him to get on the field on defense. St-Juste also plays some of the most snaps of any cornerback in the NFL, and he's expected to contribute as both a jammer on the punt return unit and as a gunner on the punt unit, two premier roles in the kicking game.

While rookie sixth-round pick Trey Smack has had his struggles during practices, he was perfect in the preseason on both field goals and PATs. The only real hiccup he had was on the first kickoff against the Denver Broncos in Week 2 of the preseason, when he kicked the ball too deep on a kickoff, which he said was due to the elevation. Otherwise, he did well on the kickoff unit, too.

Trey Smack did a good job kicking to returners pinned deep and near the numbers. pic.twitter.com/xSzmfLbXsJ

He, obviously, will be the Packers' starting kicker for the 2026 season.

MarShawn Lloyd's preseason carries pic.twitter.com/GjErUGGTkE

Beyond the 15 truly new Green Bay Packers, the 4 players above deserve honorable mention notes as new Packers for the 2026 season, since they didn't play a single game in 2025. Running back MarShawn Lloyd, offensive lineman John Williams and offensive lineman Travis Glover were injured for the entire 2025 regular season, despite them being members of the Packers' active roster at some point last year. Defensive lineman Anthony Campbell, maybe the MVP of training camp, was added to Green Bay's practice squad going into the postseason, so he was technically, by the skin of his teeth, a member of the 2025 team, too.

If you want to say that there are 19 new Packers on the 53-man roster, not 15, I won't argue with you.

title: Noles News: FSU was plus 4 in the turnover margin and still lost
description: FSU enters the bye with more questions than answers on defense and not a lot of time to solve them
fullText:
Florida State's defense gave up 585 yards for an average of 8.7 yards per play and dropped the first ACC game of the season 27-24 to SMU.

Final.#NoleFamily pic.twitter.com/MVmqTIDUdf

Florida State will have to take a desperate look at its passing game this bye week if they want to have any shot of making a bowl game this year. The consensus among staff members is that your starter is at quarterback will not give you any chance at any real success this season.

FSU reportedly spent $650k for Tre Wisner out of the portal, he had zero snaps played last night. You could've spent that money for a more competent quarterback.

Speaking of high-priced players, Mandrell Desir has recorded two solo tackles through two games; maybe he's ready for basketball season:

Please watch #3 for FSU right before the defense gives up a 30 yard gain on 3rd & 10 😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/6vKtVqRr7A

Nice to see these two on the sidelines last night:

title: Can Ismael Saibari develop into a dependable backup to Harry Kane at Bayern Munich?
description: FC Bayern likes Ismael Saibari, but can he be the man behind the man?
fullText:
Harry Kane remains the undisputed No. 9 in Vincent Kompany's squad, but Bayern Munich will need a reliable option behind him across a long and demanding season.

That is where Ismaël Saibari could become particularly interesting.

The Moroccan international brings versatility, athleticism, technical quality, and the ability to play in multiple attacking roles. While he is not a like-for-like replacement for Kane, his skill set could give Kompany another option when Kane needs a rest or when Bayern Munich need a different attacking profile.

So far, however, the results have been mixed (at best) for Saibari in the No. 9 role.

The bigger question is whether Saibari can develop the consistency, movement, finishing, and physical presence required to handle the expectations of playing as Kane's backup at Bayern Munich.

He does not need to become another Harry Kane(who is?). Saibari simply needs to become a player Kompany trusts when Kane is unavailable or needs a breather.

Could Saibari grow into that role and give Bayern Munich the dependable striker depth they need?

title: Fairfield Prep football ready for 162-mile journey for opener at Scranton Prep (Pa.)
description: Fairfield Prep's opener will be against Scranton Prep (Pa.), which has already played two games.
fullText:
It's not the destination but the journey.

And for the Fairfield Prep football team, the opening week of the 2026 season will truly be a journey.

The Jesuits are gearing up for an approximately 162-mile trip to Pennsylvania to take on Scranton Prep to kick off the new season. It will be a two-day excursion for Fairfield Prep, which will leave via bus on Thursday with the game set for  6 p.m., Friday.

The Cavaliers will visit Fairfield Prep next fall.

Taking a long road trip could be a boon for what is a relatively young Jesuits team.

"It's the first out-of-state game for all of us and the team's really pumped up," said senior lineman Reece Morgan. "They're coming to our house next year so that's going to fun for the younger guys but we're excited to go there. We're ready for the challenge and just counting down the days."

Fairfield Prep had been hoping to start a tradition of playing at least one out-of-state team, coach Keith Hellstern said, preferably facing a Jesuit or Catholic high school.

Scranton Prep and coach Terry Gallagher had reached out to Hellstern and the Jesuits a few years ago and that interest led to an agreement between the two programs for a home and home series.

The showdown in Pennsylvania trip is part of a high-octane start for the Jesuits, who will follow that opener with games against three straight CIAC champions: At New Canaan (Class L), and home against Sheehan (Class S) and Hand (Class SS).

"We set this up in advance, a home and home, and we're excited about the opportunity," Hellstern said. "It's exciting for the guys to be able to do it. It's going to be a challenge because we have a very tough beginning of the season. Scranton Prep is an excellent program and then we have a great slate with no easy games coming up. We've done a great job concentrating on a daily basis and just getting better."

The game is part of the Connecticut High School Football Alliance schedule, which features three out-of-state games in Week 1. Norwich Free Academy plays at Westerley (R.I.) at 7 p.m., Friday, and Hand plays at Bishop Hendricken (R.I.) at 6 p.m., Saturday.

Fairfield Prep beat Bishop Hedricken 27-7 two seasons ago, and was edged by Belen (Fla.) 15-14 in the 2022 opener. Both of those games were at Rafferty Stadium in Fairfield.

Part of the challenge in playing Scranton Prep stems from the fact that the Cavaliers will have played two games this season. They lost at Loyola Blakefield (Md.) 41-34 on Aug. 28, and host Trinity (Pa.) in their second game.

"They've played one Jesuit High School already from Maryland and that's a very good program," Hellstern said. "They lost a tight one but they were very competitive. They're scrappy and physical. As far as that part of northeastern PA is concerned for their division, they're one of the best teams in thar area. So we know we're going to have a fight."

The Jesuits are hoping having an opportunity to see what Scranton Prep looks like in action can play to their advantage.

"We're watching a lot of film and we're taking advantage of the games they've played before us," senior wide receiver Dakota Newton said. "We're using that to really get deep into the team and find out how we can take the best approach against them."

Hellstern said the team will possibly have a walk-through practice on Thursday before departing for Pennsylvania.

The bus ride will likely take three to three and a half hours. Once they arrive, the coach said, the Jesuits plan to settle in, have a team dinner, and watch the 49ers and Rams play in an NFL Thursday night game.

After breakfast Friday, the Jesuits will have meetings, go to mass and do another walk-through with the game on tap that evening.

It's a unique experience for the players and one they're ready for.

"It's super-fun to start this way," senior Brody Sommers said. "Going down Thursday is going to give us enough time to prepare, get a good sleep and be with the boys on Thursday night and then Friday, everything is going into that game.

"We haven't been part of (a long road trip), but everyone is super excited to be part of it. It's going to be great."

title: A look at Connecticut's longest-tenured active football coaches as Lou Marinelli nears 400 wins
description: As the 2026 football season approaches, we take a look at the longest-tenured active CIAC high school football coaches.
fullText:
Four years ago, while working on GametimeCT's high school football previews, a couple of coaches stood out because they had been head coaches at the same school for a long time.

I decided to put together a list of the 10 longest-tenured football head coaches in the state. This year that list has been updated, with 15 coaches because of ties.

Five coaches have stepped down in the last four seasons and one took a head coaching job at another school.

Reminder: This list ranks the longest-tenured coaches at one school without interruption.

No. 1 LOU MARINELLI, NEW CANAAN, 45th season

Since this list was first released four years ago, all Marinelli and the Rams have done is win. He has won four state titles over those four seasons and has gone 49-3.

His 16 state titles equal the combined total of the next nine coaches on this list.

Marinelli is one win away from reaching 400 career wins at New Canaan.

No. 2 ANTHONY SAGNELLA, NORTH HAVEN, 29th season

It's been a good four years for the North Haven football program.

In the first edition of this list, the number next to state titles was zero. Over the next two seasons, that number grew to two.

While the team hasn't reached the postseason the past two seasons, Sagnella always has his team contending for a spot.

No. 3 JOE DELLA VECCHIA, ST. JOSEPH, 28th season

Della Vecchia rounds out the top three, which is unchanged from the first edition of the list.

He has led the Hogs to four more playoff appearances, one state title and a 34-13 record since 2022.

No. 4 PAT SMITH, PLAINFIELD/QUINEBAUG VALLEY, 26th season

Smith makes the first jump in this list. He was No. 5 in 2022, but following the retirements of Ridgefield's Kevin Callahan and Hall's Frank Robinson III, he moves up a spot.

He has guided Plainfield into a new co-op with the Quinebaug Valley program and reached the postseason in 2025.

No. 5 CHAD NEAL, KILLINGLY, 22nd season

Neal stands alone at No. 5 following A.J. Massengale's departure from Stonington after the 2025 season and Mark Basil's retirement at North Branford.

Killingly has continued to win under Neal, adding four postseason appearances and another state title over the past four seasons.

TIE-No. 6 JOHN FERRAZZI, SHEEHAN, 21st season

Ferrazzi is the second-longest tenured coach in the SCC and has continued to build the Titans into a small-school powerhouse.

Over the last four seasons, he has led the team to three playoff appearances and won his second state title. In the last two seasons, the Titans have gone 21-5.

TIE-No. 6 CHRIS SARLO, KENNEDY, 21st season

Since the first edition of this list was released, Sarlo and Kennedy have posted two of the program's best seasons since he took over in 2005.

He had his first winning season when the Eagles finished 6-4 in 2023. In 2024, the team went 7-4, which included the program's first playoff appearance.

No. 8 TANNER GROVE, MONTVILLE/ST. BERNARD, 20th season

Four years ago, Grove was tied with former Ansonia coach Tom Brockett, who retired before the 2025 season.

Grove now stands alone in eighth place as he heads into his 20th season.

It's been rough for Montville over the last four years, as the team has gone 7-33. However, St. Bernard has joined the program, giving it more players.

No. 9 JASON BRUENN, PLATT, 19th season

Bruenn was tied with John Acquavita, who was at Wilbur Cross when this list came out in 2022. Acquavita stepped down after that season and took the job at Newington.

Over the last four seasons, Platt has returned to the playoffs once, and Bruenn has claimed his 100th career win.

No. 10 SCOTT SALIUS, GILBERT/NORTHWESTERN/HOUSATONIC, 18th season

Salius is the newest member of the top 10, having just missed the previous cutoff by one season. Now, he is firmly on the list.

Over his career at Gilbert, Salius has won 106 games and led the program to five playoff appearances. He has also guided them through a couple of changes - the addition of Housatonic and the move from the Pequot Conference to the NVL.

title: ‘I can’t handle this’ – Chargers fans react to Justin Herbert injury scare in latest practice
description: Los Angeles Chargers fans have been left concerned about Justin Herbert’s safety following a bizarre incident in practice. The Chargers get their season up and running on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals – a game they will be expected to win comfortably.
fullText:
Los Angeles Chargers fans have been left concerned about Justin Herbert's safety following a bizarre incident in practice.

The Chargers get their season up and running on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals – a game they will be expected to win comfortably.

However, any success the Chargers enjoy this season will largely rely on the health and quality of their quarterback, Herbert.

It has been a busy offseason for Herbert, who has been thrown even further into the public spotlight through his relationship with Madison Beer.

The game at SoFi Stadium on Sunday was almost put under question for Herbert after a near miss with a camera operator during Monday's practice session.

Touching the quarterback in practice is as big of a no-go for head coaches as there ever will be.

You only have to watch the latest series of Hard Knocks, where Mike Macdonald lost his cool with Seattle Seahawks defender Derrick Hall for getting too close to Sam Darnold.

During the latest Chargers' practice, it was actually a staff member who almost collided with Herbert as he snapped the ball.

'Someone nearly got fired,' replied one relieved Chargers fan.

'Bro I can't handle this rn,' said another just days out from the season opener.

Thankfully, there was no collision between the camera operator and Herbert, with the member of staff seen holding up his hand in apology following the close call.

Another fan responded: 'This would be the most Chargers thing ever if Herbert got injured from this.'

Whilst another said: 'Welp that's one way to lose your job'.

Sunday will offer Chargers fans their first real look at what Mike McDaniel has been creating behind the scenes as the new offensive coordinator.

It could have been so much different had Herbert sustained an injury through this close call, though.

'Even the camera guys get pressure on Herbert,' one fan found the funny side of the incident.

'Heart flashed before my eyes,' said another relieved Chargers fan.
