title: Horse Tracks: Payton expects Mahomes, Chiefs to be full strength on MNF
description: Good morning, Broncos Country! We are FINALLY kicking off Week 1 of the 2026 season and Broncos against Chiefs on Monday Night Football could not be a better way to do it. And whatever hope you have that the Chiefs will trot out a hobbled Patrick Mahomes in Week 1 after spending the offseason recovering […]
fullText:
We are FINALLY kicking off Week 1 of the 2026 season and Broncos against Chiefs on Monday Night Football could not be a better way to do it.

And whatever hope you have that the Chiefs will trot out a hobbled Patrick Mahomes in Week 1 after spending the offseason recovering from a season-ending ACL tear last year, Sean Payton has some advice for you.

Just stop (because he "answered this last week").

"I think we're looking at it and expecting someone who's 100 percent, someone who's moving well based on what limited footage you get," Payton admitted. "He's going to be one of those guys that threatens you not only in the pocket, but out of the pocket."

"We're expecting someone who's 100 percent. …You have to be ready and prepare for what you know is his best, and that's in the pocket, that's the extended plays, that's him running."

Basically, the head coach said, prepare for vintage Mahomes.

"Our approach has been pay close attention to what we've seen historically film-wise, how we defend not only him, but their team," the head coach added. "I think you have to be ready and prepare for what you know is his best, and that's in the pocket, that's the extended plays, that's him running."

And often finding an open target, much to the dismay of the defensive backs.

But Patrick Surtain II and his fellow DBs have been focusing on takeaways this offseason, so they are looking forward to showcasing the hard work.

"I think it's all about intention. It's one thing to think about turnovers, but it's being intentional at the same time," Surtain II said. "When you're going to the ball, you're intentional about stripping the ball out, about intercepting the ball. I think that's what matters because we all have the ability. We all could get a takeaway, we all could pick the ball, but it's all about a mindset going in towards a play and actually capitalizing on those opportunities."

Workin' towards Week 1️⃣ pic.twitter.com/9dCODNBvpe

And with the addition of Kenneth Walker III to the running back room, the Broncos' run defense may have to be as strong as its pass defense when facing the Chiefs.

"I think [Walker III] has really good contact balance, vision with home-run speed," Payton said. "He's a heck of a football player."

But perhaps one of the toughest matchups for Payton when facing the Chiefs is squaring off against defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo.

"Steve [Spagnuolo] has always done a great job disguising looks, giving you zone-pressure looks," Payton said. "He's not afraid to play zero. You're going to have to have a real good protection plan and be disciplined in your approach, especially when you're facing that defense on the road with the noise."

"Every game is tough. …You have to forget about what happened last season, because every season's completely different. …The division's open for whoever to take at this point."

Since the Broncos have won the last three matchups against the Chiefs, it would be easy to be lulled into thinking this rivalry — and this division — is the Broncos' to lose.

But no one in the building is thinking that. Every year is a new season with new challenges — and new challengers.

"This is a very tough division," said offensive guard Quinn Meinerz. "Every game is tough. … You kind of have to have short-term memory. You have to forget about what happened last season, because every season's completely different. We have a new team. They have a new team. The division's open for whoever to take at this point."

Meinerz added that each season the team has prove itself all over again.

"That's something we have to do again this year. That's just kind of the nature of the beast of the NFL is everyone kind of resets and gets ready for the next season," Meinerz added. "I think we've done a good job resetting. We know they've done a great job as well. They're a really well-coached team. It's going to be AFC West football."

This time, next week. ⏳ pic.twitter.com/M67lAofEdW

"I'm ready and I'm patient," Jebbison said. "I'll get my chance and every minute I get, every second or whatever, I'll work my hardest so that's what I'm trying to do, just take it day-by-day.

title: Today in Boston Celtics history: Marvin Barnes passes; John Thomas born
description: Today in Boston Celtics history, Marvin Barnes passed away in 2014.
fullText:
Today in Boston Celtics history, Marvin Barnes passed away in 2014. A native of Providence, Rhode Island, Barnes was born in 1952 in the smallest of all of the United States. He played his NCAA basketball for the Providence College Friars before the Philadelphia 76ers picked him up with the second overall selection of the 1974 NBA Draft.

The Rhode Islander elected to sign with the Spirits of St. Louis of the American Basketball Association (ABA) instead of signing with the Sixers, playing for that franchise for two seasons before joining the Detroit Pistons in 1976 after the Spirits of St. Louis dispersal draft. The dispersal draft was the result of the ABA-NBA merger when that team did not join the NBA. The Pistons trade Barnes to the Buffalo Braves in 1977, who in turn dealt him to the Celtics in 1978.

Barnes played 38 games for Boston in the 1978-79 season, averaging 8.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game while with the team.

It is also the birthday of former Boston big man John Thomas, born today in Minneapolis, Minnesota, in 1975. A standout with the University of Minnesota, Thomas was drafted by the New York Knicks with the 25th pick of the 1995 NBA Draft. He never suited up for New York, however. He was dealt with Dontae' Jones, Walter McCarty, and Scott Brooks (yes, that Scott Brooks) to the Celtics in exchange for Chris Mills and draft assets.

Thomas played only 33 games for Boston in the 1997-98 season. In them, he averaged 3.3 points and 2.1 boards before being traded with Chauncey Billups, Dee Brown, and Roy Rogers to the Toronto Raptors for Kenny Anderson, Popeye Jones, and Žan Tabak in 1998.

title: Christian Gonzalez signs historic new deal with Patriots
description: Christian Gonzalez has signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension with the New England Patriots, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.
fullText:
Christian Gonzalez has signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension with the New England Patriots, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz was the first to report the deal, which includes $102 million guaranteed.

Gonzalez's new contract is $3 million more than the deal signed by Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon, who held the distinction of being the NFL's highest-paid cornerback after signing his extension last month. Gonzalez and Witherspoon share the same agent.

The massive contract comes as the Patriots get ready to open the NFL season on the road against the Seahawks in Seattle. New England will have Gonzalez on the field for the season opener, giving the Patriots one of their most important defensive players as they begin the new campaign.

Gonzalez celebrated the news on Instagram overnight, posting a photo with the caption, "Thank you Lord! PATS NATION LET'S GO."

The 24-year-old cornerback had been a full participant for most of Patriots training camp, but his contract situation remained one of the biggest questions surrounding the team throughout the summer. Gonzalez routinely faced questions from reporters about the status of negotiations as the two sides worked toward a new deal.

At the beginning of training camp, Patriots owner Robert Kraft said the team had offered Gonzalez a contract that would make him the highest-paid player at his position.

Before agreeing to the extension, Gonzalez was under contract with the Patriots for two more seasons and was scheduled to earn a little more than $20 million during that time. The new agreement instead makes him the centerpiece of a record-setting contract at the cornerback position.

Despite his importance to the defense, Gonzalez was not named among the Patriots' captains for this season. Still, his role on the field remains critical as New England prepares for a difficult opening matchup against Seattle.

The Seahawks have their own star cornerback in Witherspoon, creating an interesting backdrop for the season opener after Gonzalez surpassed him as the NFL's highest-paid player at the position.

title: Trent Green discusses the Chiefs' offense with Kenneth Walker III
description: During his interview with @EdEastonJr, former Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Trent Green discussed the Chiefs' offense with Kenneth Walker III
fullText:
This week, Chiefs Wire's Ed Easton Jr. spoke with TV Analyst and former Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Trent Green.

In his interview with Easton Jr., Green joined the unveiling of the Dr Pepper "Fan Wall of Fame" painting on the side of the Alumni Hall building at his alma mater, Indiana University, curated by Indianapolis artist Nate Baranowski. He discussed the offseason addition of running back Kenneth Walker III to the offense.

"The first Dr Pepper Fan Wall of Fame will be unveiled," said Green. "It celebrates fans across college football, especially here in Bloomington, and marks last year's national championship and the start of this year's season."

For all the college football fans in Bloomington, IN…we’re cooking up something with @natebaranowski for this weekend 👀 pic.twitter.com/GBMgTFFE0I

Green orchestrated some explosive offenses during his six seasons in Kansas City. He weighed in on Walker's addition and how it will contribute to this year's offense.

"Well, I think there are just different ways to attack it, and I think the three Super Bowl championships and the five Super Bowl appearances show that you can do it without a 1,000-yard rusher," said Green, "and how offenses have spread out over the last decade. I see that trend changing a little bit more. I say that because if you look at last year with the Seattle Seahawks that won the Super Bowl, Denver (Broncos), New England (Patriots), the (Los Angeles) Chargers, teams that like to get underneath center and do more of the running game, play multiple tight end packages."

Over the past few seasons, Kansas City has relied on its defense because its offense hasn't produced many explosive plays. Mahomes' early seasons saw the unit rank among the best in the NFL regularly.

"Defenses have adapted over the last decade to doing more bubble coverage, so they get four deep, and then on the snap they rotate," said Green. "Whether they drop the safeties, whether they rotate the safeties, whether they roll to one corner, whatever it is, they're making it hard to get the big plays. There are fewer big plays now than what we're kind of in that, we still think of the high-flying Chiefs with Tyreek Hill and Patrick Mahomes and throwing 50 touchdowns and those kinds of things. I think the league has adjusted to that."

Walker was signed during the offseason after leading the Seattle Seahawks to victory over the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LX, earning game MVP honors with 27 carries for a season-high 135 yards and 26 receiving yards.

"As much as anything, you want to focus on the tight ends and the run game and the underneath passes in that 10 to 15 to 20 yarder in the middle of the field, maybe a slant or a drag underneath if you if you get some depth of the of the underneath coverage," said Green, "I think all those things are going to happen I think I think you'll see Patrick under under center more because of the offensive evolve the way the offense has evolved I think it is going to be huge for for Kenneth Walker this year I think they are going to find ways to use him in the passing game not just in the screen game which is something that he's very capable of. Still, I think they're going to find different ways to get him involved in the pass game as well. But running the football is going to be a vital part of this Chiefs offense this year."

title: Brundle doubles down on Hamilton-Leclerc clash verdict after Rosberg debate
description: Martin Brundle doubled down on his verdict regarding the clash between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton at the Italian Grand Prix. After the conclusion of the Italian Grand Prix, the former Formula 1 driver debated the incident with 2016 world champion Nico Rosberg.
fullText:
Martin Brundle doubled down on his verdict regarding the clash between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton at the Italian Grand Prix.

After the conclusion of the Italian Grand Prix, the former Formula 1 driver debated the incident with 2016 world champion Nico Rosberg. The German said that the Turn 1 incident after the start of the race was clearly Leclerc's fault.

In his column for Sky Sports, Brundle addressed the situation once again and stood by his initial thoughts.

He wrote: "Into the first chicane Hamilton released the brakes and rolled up the inside of Leclerc, forcing him wide and meaning a tight entry into the immediate Turn 2.

"They were side by side and Hamilton stuck it out around the outside. A likely miffed Leclerc understeered wide on that inside line and nerfed Hamilton off into the gravel. He could have given him more room most likely but clearly didn't want to."

Martin Brundle - Photo: Race Pictures

He continued: "There are necessarily comprehensive rules of engagement in general combat, and chicanes are often treated as one corner in that respect, but the whole scenario is seen through a different lens with the inevitable close contact on the opening lap. After all, we enjoy starting them as a tight pack."

The stewards did not penalize Leclerc for the incident. "Whatever the rules, if you're on the outside of Turn 2 in Monza at any point, you're highly likely to be run out of road and end up high on the exit kerb or in the gravel. We've all been there," Brundle concluded.

The seven-time world champion had a clear verdict after the Monza incident. He told GPblog, among others: "Look, you know, I don't race dirty. I've always raced clean and fairly and always left space. And so I don't think they should be worried about me. I mean, I've come into the team and tried to be respectful of space and definitely not put the team in jeopardy.

"And I stand by that, and I that's all I can talk about is on my side. You have to speak to Fred [Vasseur] about the other side and decisions that that are taken there. But I'll keep pushing and trying to get more from the team and from my car and from the engineers and design and everything like that."

title: Southern Heritage Classic events in Memphis go beyond the game
description: The annual Southern Heritage Classic returns for its 37th year with a mix of football, music and community events in Memphis.
fullText:
The annual Southern Heritage Classic — a mix of football, music and community — returns for its 37th year with events running Sept. 11-12 in Memphis.

Launched in 1990 by Memphis businessman Fred Jones Jr., the Classic has become one of the Mid-South's longest-running and most vibrant cultural celebrations, having grown from a spirited gridiron battle to a multifaceted community event.

Built around an annual football game between Historically Black Colleges and Universities, 2026 sees the rivalry continue between the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions and Alcorn State Braves. The big game will take place Sept. 12 at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium.

As part of the 2026 Classic, there will be numerous events including a college and career fair, a fashion show, a parade and golf tournament, plus various other festivities leading up to the game. Here are some of the highlights.

8:30 a.m.-2 p.m. Sept. 11; Memphis Sports & Events Center, 995 Early Maxwell Blvd. in Liberty Park

Presented by the City of Memphis Office of Youth Services, this event will feature regional college and university representatives as well as businesses on hand to provide information about attending school and employment opportunities. Admission is free. 

MEMPHIS ENTERTAINMENT NEWS: John Doyle leaving Rock 'n' Soul Museum, Memphis Music Hall of Fame

8 a.m. Sept. 12; Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium parking lots and Tiger Lane

It's all about friends, food and football at this ticketed tailgate event. Tickets and packages are available at Ticketmaster.com.

Bluff City hoops legend and University of Memphis Tigers head coach Penny Hardaway will host an $800-per-team, 4-man scramble golf event at Tunica National Golf and Tennis. All participants receive a golf shirt and gift bag with premium items. For information, call (901) 265-4886 or visit Memphisdistrictgolfclassic.org.

The Orange Mound Community Parade Committee presents its salute to the Southern Heritage Classic. The parade route runs along Park Avenue from Haynes Street to Airways Boulevard. The parade will feature marching bands, civic organizations, businesses and more. For information, contact Claudette Boyd at (901) 413-7109 or visit omcpc.org.

The competition will feature the best high school show bands in the region with show-stopping dance routines. Tickets: $12 advance; $15 day of. To purchase tickets or 

11 a.m. Sept. 12; The Great Hall, 1900 S. Germantown Road

The theme for the annual Classic Fashion Show & Brunch is "Crowned in Heritage." The event is presented by the National Coalition of 100 Black Women Inc. — Memphis Chapter. Tickets: $100. To purchase tickets or for information, call (901) 568-4021 or visit Memphisncbw.org.

6 p.m. Sept. 12; Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium

Experience the continuing football rivalry featuring Arkansas-Pine Bluff vs. Alcorn State. The proceedings will also include the AutoZone Halftime Show, featuring ASU's Sounds of Dyn-O-Mite and UAPB's Marching Musical Machine of the Mid-South. After the game, stay for the Classic 5th Quarter, the grand finale for the Southern Heritage Classic with a battle of the bands. All seats are reserved. Tickets: $23-$53; go to Ticketmaster.com.

title: “Mike Trout Is Going to Have One of the Wildest Careers in Sports History” – Fans React as Angels Are Eliminated From Playoff Contention
description: Angels’ star Mike Trout has now gone 12 years with the club without appearing in the postseason. After the Halos lost the series opener to the Red Sox at Fenway Park on Monday, the team was eliminated from playoff contention for the 12th straight season.
fullText:
Angels' star Mike Trout has now gone 12 years with the club without appearing in the postseason. After the Halos lost the series opener to the Red Sox at Fenway Park on Monday, the team was eliminated from playoff contention for the 12th straight season.

Trout's last postseason appearance was in 2014, when the Angels were eliminated in the ALDS after losing the first three games to the KC Royals. After Stan Kroenke agreed to buy the team from Arte Moreno in a reported $4 billion deal, fans discussed Trout's future and loyalty, with him turning 36 next year.

Trout will likely be the best player of his generation never to win the Commissioner's Trophy if LA, under Kroenke, can't secure a title soon. Fans echoed similar sentiments on social media after the Angels were eliminated from playoff contention this season.

"Just an absolute WASTE of Mike Trout," one fan commented.

Trout went 1-for-4 in the series opener against the Red Sox, while Adley Rutschman and Jarren Duran powered Boston to a crucial win as the race for the AL Wild Card spots heats up. The Halos sit at the bottom of the AL West standings with a 54-90 record, the worst in the league.

Mike Trout is posting decent numbers on offense this year despite the Halos' lackluster campaign. Given that the numbers do not reflect his peak years in the league, they still offer some hope in what was otherwise yet another heartbreaking campaign by the 2002 World Series champions.

Trout has a .243 batting average, 20 home runs, 51 RBIs, and a .799 OPS in 125 games this year. He is projected to hit 23 home runs and drive in 58 runs this season.

Fans are hopeful that the new owners will create positive changes within the clubhouse. However, only time will reveal if their star can secure the elusive title before his career ends.

title: Former ref explains Arsenal-Chelsea red-card decision
description: Dermot Gallagher has backed the referee’s decision not to send off Gabriel Magalhaes for a kick to Emi Martinez’s head, explaining that the defender got the ball.Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesA...
fullText:
Arsenal won 2-1 against Chelsea on Sunday, but some Chelsea fans were incensed by what they believed to be a red-card offence ignored by the referee.

Gabriel Magalhaes and Emi Martinez were among a throng of players on the floor attempting to play the ball, but the Arsenal defender's kick ended up catching Martinez in the head with his follow-through.

It was a glancing blow at best, but some have argued it was deserving of a red card. Speaking to Sky Sports, former referee Dermot Gallagher and his co-hosts disagreed.

"They're all on the floor. There's a big tangle. He definitely goes to kick the ball and he gets the ball," Gallagher pointed out.

"That's why it pops out of Martinez's hands. Then his foot goes up and catches Martinez in the head. I don't think there's any malice whatsoever in that."

Tim Sherwood agreed, saying: "I think his foot slipped off the top of the ball and caught Martinez. I think Martinez makes far too much of it. That is the red flag."

Making their views unanimous, Jay Bothroyd added: "I didn't think that would be a red card at all."

On the other controversial moments in the game, Gallagher felt Declan Rice did foul Morgan Rogers as the Chelsea attacker ran towards goal, but that it didn't meet the threshold for a red-card VAR intervention.

"Rice clearly flicks out at him and brings him down, but the VAR can only say it's a red card or nothing," Gallagher explained. "Is it a red card? No. If the referee had seen it, he'd have given a foul."

Finally, Gallagher believed that a potential foul on Rogers in the build-up to Arsenal's winning goal was a debatable decision, but that it was too long before the goal for the game to be called back.

"He [the ref] didn't think it was a foul. Is it a foul? Debatable," Gallagher said. "The game has gone on and on, so has that impacted the move? Arsenal have won the ball in their own half. Once you start getting the VAR to go in there, you've no longer got a referee."

Sherwood went one further, suggesting it wasn't a foul to begin with.

"Morgan Rogers has just thrown himself down," Sherwood insisted. "He [Konsa] just strengths him off. That is not a foul."

Overall, it seems the Sky Sports trio had very little sympathy for Chelsea, with a yellow card for Rice likely to be the worst that could have happened. There was no cause for a red card, nor for Arsenal's goals to be ruled out.

title: Copley grad Landon Robinson begins Bengals career armed with powerful cause
description: Landon Robinson and his mother are in lockstep about the importance of the defensive tackle maximizing his ability to reach people as an NFL player.
fullText:
Landon Robinson called his mother with life-changing news last week while she was driving.

A Copley High School graduate, Robinson had just been told he made the Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster, and the defensive tackle from the United States Naval Academy wanted to share the development with his proud mom, Patrice Robinson. But when the son and mother connected through FaceTime, it took a few seconds for Landon Robinson to spit out the positive update because tears of joy took control.

"I just really just let it all flow and really felt all the emotions of what just happened," Landon Robinson recently told the Beacon Journal by phone.

Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year

It's fitting for Robinson to reach out to his mom before anyone else. They are in lockstep about the importance of Robinson maximizing his platform as an NFL player and using it for the greater good. In April, they created the Landon Robinson Foundation, a mental health advocacy organization designed to address youth suicide.

"We don't want to waste that opportunity, for sure," Patrice Robinson, the CEO and co-founder of the Landon Robinson Foundation, said during a recent phone interview. "We want to make sure that we are able to help people just by being a light. I have a spirit and Landon has a spirit of jovialness. It's easy to be around us, and I love that. I think that's a gift from God, and I don't take it lightly."

More NFL news: Bengals select Landon Robinson in seventh round of draft

Robinson was born in Columbus, but his family moved to Fairlawn when he was in second grade. He attended Fort Island Primary School, Copley Fairlawn-Middle School and Copley High School, where he graduated in 2021.

Robinson, 23, and his mother said several high school students died by suicide during Robinson's time at Copley. Then a U.S. Naval Academy midshipman took his own life during Robinson's senior season at Navy. Shortly thereafter, Robinson started discussions with his mom about how he could impact the community in a powerful way. Brainstorming steered them toward mental health issues affecting young people.

"I've seen people struggle with mental health," Robinson said. "I've seen people make bad decisions with their mental health. Obviously, it's something that's uncomfortable to talk about, but it's something that truly needs advocacy and needs people to be speaking about it in order for it to get better.

"Even before I got drafted, my mom and I were just talking about, 'What's a way that we can help the community and we can help people?' We came up with this foundation, which is advocating for mental health and doing events to spread that wellness and just help people out in the long run."

As Patrice Robinson spoke on a panel in Rochester, New York, she gained a greater understanding about why some parents don't want to discuss youth suicide.

"There's a stigma that's attached to that. There's a shame that's attached to that," she said. "There are some people, which I was surprised to learn, but I learned that some people don't want to talk about it because they feel like it will plant the seed in their children to do it."

More NFL coverage: Nick Chubb's former Cleveland Browns teammates react to his retirement

The Robinsons aim to provide educational resources to families, and they have enlisted professionals who are qualified to spearhead the mission.

For example, Patrice Robinson's best friend, Arielle H. Sheftall, is the foundation's director of research and grant support. Landon Robinson calls Sheftall his "aunt" because of the Robinson family's close-knit relationship with Sheftall.

"Her research delved into the emotional side of things, the chemical brain makeup of these children, the social side, family, their environment and school and things of that nature," Patrice Robinson said. "... There was significant research that she did that showed that there are brain chemicals that shift at certain ages in a person's life and that when they're younger, they may exhibit some of these behaviors and some of these emotions, like depression or ADHD or so forth and so on, that if the parents could catch it young enough, they could change the trajectory of their child's life."

A reserve Marine, Landon Robinson graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy with a degree in cyber operations, and he is commissioned as a second lieutenant officer. He's well-rounded and realizes professional athletes carry a celebrity status. As an NFL player, he will likely be able to reach a larger audience than the average person.

"I've seen athletes have foundations and do things that can help people and all this stuff, but there were not too many people that really talk about the mental health side of things," said Robinson, who recalled Cavaliers legend Kevin Love speaking out on related issues.

In August, the Landon Robinson Foundation hosted a back-to-school movie night in Cincinnati. Monthly meetings with teenagers will begin later this month. Robinson envisions more community events, school visits and training sessions.

In the meantime, Robinson is preparing for his rookie season to begin in earnest. The Bengals are scheduled to open the upcoming season at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 1 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 13.

Robinson's father, Lance Robinson, is a former Kent State University gymnast who grew up near Cincinnati and is a lifelong Bengals fan. Patrice Robinson said she started "screaming" and "crying" when her second of three sons revealed he had made an NFL roster.

A seventh-round draft pick (No. 226 overall), Robinson tied for first in sacks (four) and tied for second in pressures (10) in the NFL during the preseason, according to the statistics compiled by Pro Football Focus.

"I'm super excited to get started," Robinson said. "I think it's the beginning of a long, long career, and I'm just excited to learn and grow. Obviously, you want to get out there as soon as you can, and you're eager to go make plays, but it takes time in reality, especially as a younger player. You've got to learn and you've got to grow because it's a big jump from college to the NFL. So, I'm excited to learn. I'm excited to grow."

Cincinnati isn't the only part of the state waiting for Robinson's opportunity to arrive. His supporters in Northeast Ohio are eager, too.

"When my time comes to get out there and shine, then I'm going to take full grasp of it," Robinson said.

Off the field, Robinson will be able to pour himself into his foundation for however long his playing days last and beyond.

"Having something else that's greater than yourself is a great transition from a world that is full of glamor and lights and action," Patrice Robinson. "You have this other side of who you are, and that's what I try to tell Landon. It's like, 'You are a multifaceted person. You're not one-dimensional.'"

The Landon Robinson Foundation is proof.

If you or someone you know needs mental health resources and support, please call, text or chat with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or visit 988lifeline.org for 24/7 access to free and confidential services.

title: Who's looking at increased role with Browns? These 3 could be in 2026
description: What Browns players could see their roles increase from the 2025 to the 2026 seasons? These are three candidates.

Even when Schwesinger returned, Mascarenas-Arnold found plenty of reps as the third linebacker with the other two. If that's not seeing a bigger role, then nothing qualifies.

Again, we're talking degrees and percentages when it comes to bigger roles. For Bond, at least once he returns to the field after a concussion, it's more about consistency than anything else after getting a late start with the Browns. As a rookie, he played in 16 games but less than 50% of the offensive snaps while being targeted 44 times. It was still fourth overall in targets, but it was more than 60 targets behind Jerry Jeudy among wide receivers.

This is as much about availability for Hall as anything. However, it's clear the Browns are putting more on the 2024 second-round pick's plate when they added reps at defensive end after Alex Wright's season-ending injury Aug. 20. title: Pirates recall Ronny Simon, option Nick Yorke to Indianapolis over weekend
description: The Pirates made some moves over holiday weekend.
fullText:
The Bucs made a move before Sunday's game with the Los Angeles Angels, recalling switch-hitting outfielder Ronny Simon and optioning infielder Nick Yorke to Triple-A Indianapolis.

Simon has only played in 9 games at the big-league level this season, but he's hitting .290 over just 34 plate attempts. He did not get to play in the Angles series.

Simon was tearing up the International League, however, leading the league with a .344 average and also second overall with 33 doubles. Simon also hit 7 homers, knocked in 72 RBIs and stole a whopping 35 bases. He was also second on the league with a .426 on-base percentage. Suffice it to say, the 26-year-old Simon earned the call up.

Yorke has played 40 games with the Pirates this season, hitting just .212 with 1 homer and 12 RBIs. He had just 3 hits in his last 10 games played for the Bucs. The 24-year-old Yorke is in his third season with the Pirates. He hit .232 last season and then .216 before that.

As for the Pirates, they are coming off of a series win against the Angels and have battled back to within two games of .500 at 71-73. They are certainly playing a bit better of late, yet still stand 5.5 games back of the Wild Card. Playoffs are not an impossibility. Only unlikely.

The Bucs are back in action tonight after taking off Labor Day, when they will return to action for the thre-game series with the Chicago White Sox. The Sox are currently leading their division, so this will be no easy series for the Bucs, but if they can keep it rolling, they can at least finish strong regardless of their playoff status.

title: Kenny Minchey had a historic debut for Kentucky Football
description: Kenny Minchey adds his name to an exclusive list of Kentucky quarterbacks
fullText:
Kenny Minchey spent his Saturday afternoon slinging the ball all over the field against Youngstown State in his first career start and Will Stein's debut as a head coach.

The game resulted in a 45-13 victory for Kentucky, with a fluid offense on display for Big Blue Nation.

Minchey had a historic day, leaving Saturday's game with statistics that put him on a very short list of quarterbacks in school history to accomplish the level of play he displayed Saturday.

This is the list of quarterbacks who had 300+ passing yards, four touchdown passes, a 65% completion percentage, and zero interceptions in a season opener, according to UK statistician Corey Price.

Kenny Minchey vs. Youngstown State (September 5, 2026)

Tim Couch at Louisville (September 5, 1998)

How about that? 28 years to the day since the first time that a Kentucky quarterback accomplished that incredible feat. Anytime you join a list that has Tim Couch's name on it, you're doing something right.

Minchey has set the bar pretty high with that performance in his first career start, getting the ball to nine different receivers and feeding four different targets for touchdowns.

This week, Minchey could add his name to another very short list that Couch is also already on: Beating Alabama.

.@UKFootball QBs to have 300 passing yards, 4 touchdown passes, 65% completion percentage, and 0 interceptions in a season opener:

– @kenny_minchey vs. Youngstown State (September 5th, 2026)

– @TimCouchQB at Louisville (September 5th, 1998)

title: Every-Down Linebacker Review: What the Preseason Told Us Before Week 1
description: Steve Hungarter breaks down each team's green-dot situation and highlights the linebackers he is drafting and avoiding in IDP leagues.
fullText:
No more trying to assemble linebacker depth charts like a Temu toy. We have three linebackers, two starting spots, four extra pieces and instructions that somehow skipped from Step 3 to Step 11.

The preseason is over. Put the tiny screwdriver down. It is time to see who actually stays on the field.

Over the last few weeks, we have tracked green dots, starter treatment, nickel packages, substitutions and enough linebacker rotations to make me question several life choices. Some situations became crystal clear. Others somehow became more confusing.

With Week 1 approaching, here is my final look at all 32 linebacker rooms, who I expect to stay on the field, and most importantly, who should wear the green dot.

One reminder before we start: starting linebacker does not automatically mean every-down linebacker. In IDP, we are chasing snaps. Base packages are nice. Ninety-plus percent of the defensive snaps are nicer.

Arizona spent the preseason treating the LB2 job like a Temu package. With Jack Gibbens appearing to have won it, Cody Simon is an extra LB3 piece, and we are still not completely sure the finished product is supposed to look like this. Because Arizona runs one every-down player, the rest might not matter for you in shallow leagues.

Mack Wilson is the linebacker who wears the green dot because he has an every-down role, playing every snap for this team. He is commonly regarded as a top-30 linebacker, yet one of my takes this offseason is that you could get him in the last round of the deepest of drafts for some strange reason.

Jack Gibbens appears to have won the LB2 job after Cody Simon was ahead of him earlier in camp. Gibbens eventually started alongside Wilson, and both were held out later in the preseason.

The only concern with Gibbens is whether he is truly an every-down player. When we saw the starters, he played around 70% of the snaps and came off in certain passing situations. Simon now looks like the LB3 after playing while Wilson and Gibbens were getting the night off. Give me Wilson as the every-down LB and green dot, Gibbens for deeper leagues as the LB2 with a 70-85% snap ceiling, and Simon as the dynasty stash next man up.

The final preseason game gave us more information to process here.

Atlanta decided we had not suffered enough this preseason after all. Divine Deablo is the only Falcons linebacker I am completely comfortable calling an every-down player. Atlanta has already handed him the green dot, and that is not changing. The real question is what happens next. Except for Deablo's rookie season (where he started five games), he has never played a full season. If he is my starting LB1, I would be worried about my team.

Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins rotated with the starters in the preseason finale, with Perkins actually getting the start next to Deablo. Daniels, however, spent two weeks wearing the green dot with the first-team defense while Deablo was injured and continued getting starter reps after Deablo returned.

I still lean Daniels as the LB2, but Perkins is going to make this messy. Atlanta has moved Perkins around and used him as a pass rusher, so I see him more as a Temu version of Jalon Walker-lite. Daniels has the cleaner path to becoming the second every-down LB, but until Atlanta stops rotating them, Deablo is the only one I am drafting with complete confidence.

Roquan Smith is the unquestioned centerpiece, and Teddye Buchanan looks positioned to join him when healthy. However, the Ravens' current depth chart has Trenton Simpson as the starting WLB next to Smith, with Buchanan recovering from a torn ACL.

The question is not whether Buchanan starts; it is how close he gets to every-down usage. If Baltimore keeps both linebackers on the field in nickel as expected, Buchanan could quickly turn into one of those late-round IDP picks we look back on and wonder why he was so cheap.

Buchanan has been one of my favorite late-round linebacker targets because the path to snaps is sitting right in front of him. If Baltimore gives him the second full-time job, his acquisition cost is going to look silly a few weeks from now.

No detective work required here. Let's move on.

Buffalo gave us one linebacker we can trust and then threw the rest of the depth chart into a blender. Terrel Bernard is the easy one. He is the green dot and the linebacker I expect to stay on the field in Buffalo's nickel-heavy defense. The LB2 spot is where things get interesting. Dorian Williams spent part of the preseason behind Kaleb Elarms-Orr, but then Williams didn't play in the finale while KEO did, which certainly looked like starter treatment for Williams.

I am leaning toward Williams getting the first crack at the LB2 job, but I am not convinced it stays like that, nor does that mean an every-down role. KEO played well enough to keep himself in the conversation, and Buffalo has little reason to force its second linebacker onto the field in every personnel package. Bernard is the only Bills linebacker I am confidently starting in shallow leagues. Williams is the upside gamble, KEO is the name I am keeping on my watchlist, and Week 1 should finally tell us whether either one gets enough snaps to matter.

Carolina spent the summer letting Trevin Wallace and Claudin Cherelus battle for the job next to Devin Lloyd. Then Bobby Okereke walked through the door. That tells me plenty.

Okereke immediately becomes my favorite for the LB2 job and should be capable of roughly 80-85% of the defensive snaps. I am not automatically projecting him as a true every-down linebacker, however. The player I want is still Lloyd, clearly in the every-down role. Cherelus, who has teased us with flashes and an above-15% tackle rate, should fill in for leftover snaps.

Dennis Allen likes to keep just two linebackers on the field. That is great news for T.J. Edwards and Devin Bush. Edwards always comes with injury concerns, but he will be wearing the green dot and moved well.

Devin Bush's 2025 season landed him this job, but he has been a mixed bag of nuts during his NFL career. Bush looks like the running mate. The secondary is already expected to struggle, so we need to see more of Bush and Edwards competently holding down the linebacker unit.

The Bengals have given us the rare preseason linebacker room that does not require a flowchart. Second-year players Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight are the guys. This time behind a rebuilt defensive line. Carter is another late-round gem who will receive the green dot and every-down role.

Cleveland is one of those linebacker rooms where I don't need to pull out the calculator. Carson Schwesinger is back at practice and remains the linebacker I want. He should handle the every-down role and the green dot, while veteran Quincy Williams slides into the LB2 spot next to him. After those two, Cleveland's final roster gets thin quickly, which only strengthens my confidence in the top pairing.

Williams is the interesting one. We know he can produce tackles when given snaps, and Cleveland should give him plenty of opportunities in nickel. I am not putting him in Schwesinger's neighborhood, but if Williams settles into an 80%-plus role, he's absolutely relevant again. Schwesinger is the entrée. Williams might be worth ordering as a side.

Dallas spent August giving us just enough information to make us dangerous. Dee Winters did not play in the preseason finale while Jaishawn Barham did, which certainly looks like starter treatment for Winters. DeMarvion Overshown remains the linebacker I trust most. He should handle the green dot, but the battle next to him is where things get interesting. Then Von Miller showed up.

I am still not convinced Winters owns that job for the entire season. Barham has enough talent and upside that I would rather stash him than spend much on Winters, especially if the second Dallas linebacker isn't truly every-down. Overshown is the guy for mid-shallow leagues. Winters gets the first shot, but Barham is the name sitting on my waiver-wire speed dial.

There have also been rumors and at least two released stories that Bobby Wagner expressed interest in coming to the team. In typical Dallas form, we have to see which horse they ride with. Stay tuned.

Alex Singleton highlights this section. He wore the green dot during the preseason and enters Week 1 as the Denver linebacker I am interested in for IDP. Denver has other linebackers, of course, but I am not drafting participation trophies.

Singleton has already shown us what happens when he is healthy and playing every down: tackles. Lots of them. Sometimes we spend August looking under every rock for the next breakout when there is a proven tackle machine standing directly in front of us. Don't overthink this one.

A huge portion of Justin Strnad's play produces splash plays, so I like to scoop him up in big-play scoring formats later in drafts. He seems like a decent add, but his role will be limited; he knows the team's scheme well.

Detroit has enough linebackers to start its own small country, but Jack Campbell is the only one I really care about for IDP. Campbell should be the every-down linebacker and wear the green dot, while Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Devin White fight over the work around him. The competition for that third linebacker spot even continued late into camp, with Rodriguez taking first-team reps. In leagues where your league mates can slot him in as a DL, that eligibility matters. In a 32-team league, a handful of tackles at a desolate position is sometimes all you need to win.

Believe it or not, I want all four of these players. The system favors linebackers. In the deepest of leagues, I use Barnes' DL/LB eligibility because of his SAM linebacker role.

That is great for the Lions and not nearly as exciting for our fantasy teams. Barnes' ability to move around and rush off the edge gives Detroit plenty of ways to get creative. Unless we see a second off-ball linebacker consistently staying on the field in nickel, I am not chasing the rest of this room in shallow leagues. Campbell gets the snaps, the dot and the tackle opportunity. Everyone else can fight over the leftovers.

Green Bay may have done us a favor this preseason. Zaire Franklin and Edgerrin Cooper played together throughout their starter reps, with Franklin wearing the green dot. Franklin gives Green Bay the veteran presence in the middle while Cooper gives them an athletic linebacker who can make plays all over the field.

This one is pretty clear; let's move on.

Houston apparently looked at the rest of the league's linebacker rotations and said, "We're good." Azeez Al-Shaair and Henry To'oTo'o remain the pair, and Houston's decision to extend To'oTo'o tells you how it feels about him. Al-Shaair should continue handling the green dot and remains the linebacker I want first.

To'oTo'o is where the value could be. If he is staying on the field alongside Al-Shaair in nickel, he does not need the green dot to become a useful IDP option. There is not a mystery box here. Sometimes two linebackers start, two linebackers play and fantasy managers get to enjoy their Sunday without checking personnel packages every six minutes.

Indianapolis gave everybody a turn at linebacker this preseason except the guy selling popcorn. Akeem Davis-Gaither received starter treatment in the finale; if you listened to me, you should not be shocked by this. The news, though, was that the ghost of Jaylon Carlies opened alongside him.

ADG is the closest thing I have to a preferred option. It is a weird thing to say, but I am not forcing this one. The Colts could rotate the second spot enough that nobody besides ADG becomes consistently useful, and we might even see the green dot remain with Camryn Bynum at safety. This is exactly why Week 1 snap counts exist so we can revisit and see where everything lands.

Jacksonville spent the entire preseason teasing us with Ventrell Miller versus Branson Combs and then refused to give us a proper ending. Neither played in the finale, which makes the situation even more interesting.

Foyesade Oluokun remains the easy part. He is the every-down linebacker, the green dot, and the guy I am drafting without losing any sleep.

I am leaning Miller for the first shot next to Oluokun, but Combs made enough noise that I am not treating the job as permanent. Until we see it, Oluokun gets the steak dinner in all formats, while Miller and Combs can split the appetizer in all-IDP leagues.

Nick Bolton remains the center of Kansas City's linebacker universe. He is the green dot, the tackle producer and the linebacker I trust to stay on the field.'Drue Tranquill should remain alongside him and is a sneaky name I pick up off waivers, while Jeff Bassa has been working toward the role previously occupied by Leo Chenal.

That is an important distinction for IDP. Bolton has the clean every-down path. Tranquill can still have (close) every-down value if Kansas City keeps two linebackers on the field consistently, but Bassa's role could steal enough situational snaps to limit everybody behind Bolton. Draft Bolton. Steal Tranquill. Everything else comes with assembly instructions.

Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker spent the preseason attached at the hip, playing every snap together when the starters were on the field. Dean wore the green dot, and that is enough for me to make him the linebacker I want first from this defense.

Walker is still very interesting. If Vegas stays primarily in two-lineback nickel, both could have significant IDP value. My concern comes when the Raiders reduce to one linebacker. Dean's green-dot responsibilities make him the obvious candidate to stay on the field, leaving Walker vulnerable to losing those snaps because of his lack of coverage skills. Dean is the safer purchase; Walker is the one where I am checking the return policy.

Daiyan Henley remains the main character here. The Chargers have already identified him as the leader of the room and the player expected to wear the green dot. After everything we saw this summer, I don't see another Chargers linebacker threatening Henley's every-down workload.

The second linebacker is another tragic story. Junior Colson was cut, then Denzel Perryman was placed on injured reserve. By process of elimination, that would leave Troy Dye for the Chargers, but I am not paying for the privilege of guessing which one gets 55% of the snaps unless it is a depth role or all-IDP leagues. Give me Henley and let somebody else adopt the rest of the family.

The Rams treated their linebacker depth chart like classified government information. Nate Landman, and that is all you need to know. Omar Speights and Shaun Dolac gave us very little preseason work to evaluate, although Dolac did receive first-team opportunities. Landman remains the one I trust; he should handle the green dot.

The problem is what happens next to him. The Rams have been perfectly comfortable using dime and single-linebacker packages. That is useful to know in the NFL. It is considerably less useful when I am setting an IDP lineup. Landman is the target; everyone else needs to show me the snaps first.

Miami took one of our bigger preseason questions and answered it with a transaction. Tyrel Dodson was released during roster cuts, and rookie Jacob Rodriguez survived on the 53-man roster alongside Jordyn Brooks. That is a pretty significant development after Rodriguez spent the summer earning a larger role.

I am still viewing Brooks as the established linebacker, but Rodriguez now has a legitimate path to significant snaps. That is exactly the type of late-preseason change I am willing to gamble on. If Rodriguez gets the green dot or approaches every-down usage in Week 1, his price is going up quickly. He went from an interesting rookie stash to somebody who needs to be rostered while we find out. I was high on Rodriguez after interviewing him at the Senior Bowl. In drafts this offseason, his ADP was buried to the point that you could sneak up to get him in drafts, but I did not expect to see the rise this fast.

Blake Cashman remains the linebacker I want in Minnesota. He and Eric Wilson project as the primary pairing in Brian Flores' nickel defense, while Ivan Pace looks more like the third linebacker/base-package piece. Cashman should handle the green dot and has the cleanest path to staying on the field regardless of personnel.

Wilson is the one I am watching for shallow-league relevance. If he consistently reaches the 80-90% range, there is enough opportunity in this defense for him to matter. Pace is a good football player, but we have learned this lesson before: being good at football and being good for IDP are not one and the same.

Robert Spillane is exactly what I want from an IDP linebacker: boring in all the right ways. He took over as New England's defensive signal-caller last season, remains the leader of the room. He should wear the green dot again. When healthy, he's been a tackling machine.

Christian Elliss is the other name worth remembering. He started 13 games and recorded a career-high 94 tackles last season, and the two spent the spring working alongside each other. Spillane is the one I am drafting confidently in shallow leagues, but if New England consistently keeps Elliss on the field with him, we might have two usable linebackers here. Ellis gets a boost from me, higher than consensus, simply because of his DL/LB eligibility on Sleeper. That is a move I can get away with rather easily, especially in a tackle-friendly league.

Kaden Elliss is the linebacker I am buying. He should wear the green dot and remain on the field when New Orleans reduces to one linebacker. Pete Werner can still have value in nickel and is a recognizable name for IDP owners, but I would rather look away and not take the chance. See if anyone remembers and use that as trade bait.

Danny Stutsman is the wild-card. His role appears to be growing, which makes Werner's situation even less comfortable. Elliss gets the steak. Werner gets the side dish. Stutsman is standing next to the table asking if anybody is going to finish that.

The Giants might have one of my favorite young linebacker situations heading into the season. Tremaine Edmunds gives them the established veteran in the middle, while rookie Arvell Reese spent the preseason looking increasingly comfortable at his new position. Reese's progress has been one of the more interesting developments of the summer.

Edmunds is still the linebacker I want first and my favorite to handle the communication responsibilities, but Reese has legitimate IDP upside if the Giants turn him loose as the second every-down linebacker. I am not avoiding this LB2 situation. I am actively interested in it. Reese is exactly the kind of player who could cost considerably more after we see his Week 1 snap count.

The Jets did not make us work very hard for this one. Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood played together throughout their starter work, and Davis wore the green dot. New York enters the season with one of the more established off-ball linebacker pairings in the league.

I am comfortable with both for IDP. Davis gives you the communication role and a sturdy floor, while Sherwood has already shown the tackle production we want. If both continue playing every down, there is no need to choose sides. For once, the Jets gave us something that does not require a congressional investigation.

Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell remain the favorites, but Jeremiah Trotter Jr. spent the preseason behaving like someone who missed the memo. Baun remains the safest linebacker in the room and should handle the green dot, but those with an untrained eye might not know his analytics are on the decline. Meanwhile, Campbell has the athleticism and draft pedigree to become the other every-down option. Campbell has a newfound path to snaps, and the team is committed to play him at linebacker.

Trotter is why I am not writing Campbell's snap percentage in permanent marker yet. Philadelphia has three linebackers it can legitimately use, and that is wonderful for Vic Fangio and slightly less wonderful for us. Baun is the one I trust. Campbell is the upside play. Trotter is the guy standing behind them whispering, "give me a chance. " That is the way I have those three ranked.

The new defensive system this preseason showed us that they will be playing two linebackers on every down. Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson gave us exactly what we wanted to see. Pittsburgh used both together in its nickel package, and both stayed on the field during that preseason sample. Queen wore the green dot, but Wilson does not need it if he is going to play alongside him every down.

With Queen being that usable redraft starter, and Wilson being the young dynasty bargain, I am hoping the current arrangement stays as is.

This is one of the situations where I am willing to be aggressive on the LB2. Wilson already showed tremendous per-snap production, and now the path to volume looks considerably cleaner. As all IDP managers know already, this has not panned out yet, but the path to volume is there, and I am willing to take another chance.

Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw are back together again. Same movie, new season. I am perfectly fine watching the sequel. Warner remains the centerpiece of the defense and should continue wearing the green dot, while Greenlaw rejoins him. He is not the same player, though. Having 52 tackles in the last two seasons, largely in part due to suspensions and injuries, I tend to avoid him in drafts.

Jaden Dugger made some exciting splash plays, so I am interested in Big Three scoring. As the LB3/SAM, I'm not expecting him to threaten the primary nickel pairing. Warner is obviously the prize. Greenlaw can absolutely matter if he stays healthy and maintains the second every-down role. Sometimes the reunion tour is worth buying tickets for.

Ernest Jones might be one of the easiest green-dot calls in the league. He is the linebacker I am drafting first in Seattle and should remain glued to the field. I take him higher than the consensus, right after the top four linebackers due to his unique situation. The real preseason story was the competition behind him, where Drake Thomas appeared to gain ground while Tyrice Knight made his own statement with an excellent preseason opener.

Thomas sitting later in the preseason certainly looked like starter treatment, but I am not completely burying Knight based on that and what Knight has done in previous seasons. It was not that long ago when people thought Knight was going to be the guy.

At any rate, I do not want either player. Whoever wins the second job still has to prove Seattle will give him enough snaps to matter in shallow leagues. Jones is automatic. Thomas is the value swing. Knight is the name I refuse to delete from my watchlist in deep contests.

Tampa Bay spent the preseason hiding the answer key to an open book test. Josiah Trotter looks to start over the middle, but Alex Anzalone looks like the safest linebacker the team has. Meanwhile, SirVocea Dennis and Christian Rozeboom leave us with considerably more questions about the leftover scraps.

I am treating Anzalone as the linebacker to own until Tampa shows us otherwise. The LB2 might eventually produce value, but I am not burning a shallow-league roster spot trying to correctly guess when that is.

And the award for Linebacker Room Most Likely to Ruin My Week still belongs to Tennessee. Cedric Gray playing 13 snaps in the preseason finale was strange enough to get my attention, while Cody Barton enters Week 1 with the inside track on the green dot. Then there is rookie Anthony Hill waiting behind them.

Gray is the linebacker I am most interested in long term, but this room feels like it could change quickly. Barton might open with the dot but may not finish the season with it, and Hill is exactly the kind of rookie I am stashing where roster space allows. Barton has the job today. I am just not putting his name on the office door yet.

Washington saved one final headache for us. Frankie Luvu and Sonny Styles could both handle communication responsibilities depending on personnel, and Dan Quinn has openly discussed rotating the responsibility when substitutions occur. Apparently one green dot wasn't complicated enough.

And this is probably where I will lose some folks; I would much rather start Leo Chenal, whose LB2 role is safe for near-every-down work, as opposed to the sharing of the other two. This is a rare exception where I am staying away from both green dots and interested in the other player.

IDP Fun Fact: Luvu has been abysmal against the run, with 21 missed tackles and a terrible 20.8% missed tackle rate. There is no way he holds this job. Clever IDP owners should fade this noise. Once the season progresses, make the move to trade for Styles as he settles into the NFL and claims this role.

This article originally appeared on The Huddle: Every-Down Linebacker Review: What the Preseason Told Us Before Week 1

title: ESPN's FPI gives Oklahoma the No. 6 best chances to win the SEC
description: ESPN's FPI gives Oklahoma the SEC's sixth-best chances to win the conference in 2026.
fullText:
The Oklahoma Sooners have won 50 conference championships; however, the Sooners haven't won a conference title since 2020. That includes not winning the SEC, or even playing for an SEC title in the two years they've been in the league.

Oklahoma hopes to change that this season. It started with a strong 51-0 opening-game statement against the University of Texas at El Paso Miners. The Sooners still have the Michigan Wolverines and New Mexico Lobos before entering conference play. They start that journey by facing the back-to-back conference champion on the road, the Georgia Bulldogs. They then take on the Texas Longhorns in Dallas, who have dominated Oklahoma in three of the last four seasons.

After Oklahoma's strong showing against the Miners, its SEC championship odds have moved up. According to ESPN's Football Power Index, the Sooners have a 5% chance to win the conference title.

Oklahoma's 5% SEC championship probability may not seem high, but it ranks No. 6 in the SEC, and the most important part of the season is still ahead. Oklahoma comes in behind Texas, Georgia, LSU, Alabama, and Texas A&M.

Michigan will provide the first major test of whether the Sooners are as improved as they looked in the opener, while Georgia and Texas will offer Oklahoma two early opportunities to make a statement within the SEC.

If Oklahoma can navigate those games successfully, its increased FPI projection will start to look more meaningful. The Sooners have already shown they can dominate an inferior opponent; now they have to prove they can beat the teams standing between them and their first SEC championship appearance. That is ultimately what will determine whether Oklahoma's conference-title drought finally comes to an end.

title: Como extend contract of women’s team star Picchi after breast cancer diagnosis
description: Como have announced that women’s team player Roberta Picchi has been diagnosed with breast cancer and that the club have decided to extend the striker’s contract for another year to support her th...
fullText:
Como have announced that women's team player Roberta Picchi has been diagnosed with breast cancer and that the club have decided to extend the striker's contract for another year to support her through her recovery.

Como forward Picchi is expected to begin treatment in the coming days following a diagnosis of breast cancer. The 34-year-old was part of the Como side that earned promotion from Serie B at the end of the 2025-26 season, earning a spot in the top flight for the first time in the team's history.

AUGUST 21: Lineup team photo during omo v Juventus – Serie A Women's Cup at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on August 21, 2026 in , Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Como have confirmed in a statement on Tuesday that they will continue to offer their full support to Picchi as she undergoes treatment for breast cancer, and in a strong show of emotional and financial support, the club has decided to extend the striker's contract until the end of the 2027-28 season.

"Como 1907 can confirm that Roberta Picchi has been diagnosed with breast cancer following a series of medical examinations," read a statement on the club website.

A general view of the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium ahead of the Serie A match between against FC Internazionale at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on April 12, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

"Roberta will now begin her treatment, supported throughout by the Club's medical team, who will work closely with the specialists responsible for her care.

"Everyone at Como 1907 is alongside Roberta and will give her and her family all the support they need during the months ahead.

"As part of that continued commitment, the Club has also renewed Roberta's contract until the end of the 2027/28 season.

"At this time, we ask that Roberta's privacy is respected as she focuses on her treatment and recovery."

title: ESPN analyst makes bold prediction about Titans' free agent signee
description: ESPN analyst predicts Tennessee Titans cornerback Alontae Taylor will struggle despite his lucrative new contract.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans are about set to see how all of their offseason moves will work out when they hit the field in Week 1 against the New York Jets.

The Titans not only overhauled their coaching staff but also retooled their roster, looking completely different from previous seasons, especially on defense, where they built around Jeffery Simmons and installed Robert Saleh's attacking defensive scheme.

As everyone counts down to kickoff, no one knows how it will pan out, but ESPN's Seth Walder looked into the Titans' future and made a bold prediction about a free-agent move he sees not working out.

Bold prediction for 2026: Alontae Taylor will allow at least 1.4 yards per coverage snap -- solidly worse than average for a starting corner. That would be a tough number considering the contract (a three-year, $60 million deal) the Titans gave him in free agency.

The Titans spent a lot of money on the defensive side of the ball, especially at cornerback, where they invested heavily in Cor'Dale Flott and Alonte Taylor, and the pair did have some rough patches in the preseason. However, with the front playing vanilla and no scheming, it is hard to tell what can be taken from that action.

Taylor has been surging in the final weeks in camp, and his inside-out versatility should be more of an asset than hindrance, but until the finished product is on the field, there is no way to know how it will play out.

This article originally appeared on Titans Wire: ESPN analyst makes bold prediction about Titans' free agent signee

title: College football rankings after Week 1: Updated Coaches Poll, AP Top 25 for ACC
description: Here's a look at the updated US LBM Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 poll for Week 2 of the college football season, and where ACC teams fall in them:
fullText:
The first full week of the 2026 college football season just concluded, and over the course of several days, the ACC made its presence felt on the national stage.

No. 7 Miami, the reigning national runner-up and the conference's preseason favorite, demolished Stanford 45-6, behind five touchdown passes from Darian Mensah and three touchdown receptions from Malachi Toney. No. 20 SMU overcame a late start — literally — to outlast Florida State, 27-24.

Louisville lost to No. 10 Mississippi, 41-38, on a 48-yard field goal as time expired, but watched as first-year starting quarterback Lincoln Kienholz racked up 376 total yards and three touchdowns.

REQUIRED READING: Dabo Swinney says Clemson football will have 'great season' after career-worst loss to LSU

Pitt earned a commanding 59-14 win over a Miami (Ohio) team expected to contend for the MAC championship, thanks to an ACC-record seven touchdown passes from budding sophomore superstar Mason Heintschel. Virginia Tech drubbed VMI, 73-3, in James Franklin's debut as the Hokies' head coach.

On a much less positive note for the conference, No. 23 Clemson was shellacked by No. 13 LSU, 51-10, a result that has intensified scrutiny of the program's direction under longtime coach Dabo Swinney.

title: Swansea's golden boot winner yet to kick-start season
description: Zan Vipotnik is backed to return to form for Swansea City, even though the striker is still not guaranteed to return to the starting side.
fullText:
Zan Vipotnik has been backed to return to form for Swansea City – even though the striker is still not guaranteed to return to the starting line-up.

Swansea are flying in the Championship, leading the table after five games, and they take their unbeaten start to Southampton on Tuesday (19:45 BST).

And yet their leading goalscorer of last season has not got up and running.

Vipotnik, 24, took the second-tier golden boot with 23 league goals last term for a side that did not trouble the eventual race for the play-offs.

The tally was built on an eye-catching start where he had bagged five goals from the opening six games.

The same number of appearances into the 2026-27 season, and Vipotnik is still to find the net.

The latest chance came in the latter stages of Saturday's goalless Welsh derby with Wrexham, Vipotnik having looked lively off the bench, but unable to steer his stretch past Anthony Patterson to break the deadlock.

Swans boss Vitor Matos, though, appears calm.

Asked whether he expected the Slovenia international to find confidence and form soon, he replied: "I think if someone knows how to score goals it's him, so I think it's just a matter of scoring."

The obvious difference is that Vipotnik has only been given one league start so far this year, with Adam Idah preferred in every game since the opening day win at Stoke City.

Idah, a £6m signing from Celtic a year ago, missed most of last season with injury, but has made his mark with two goals so far.

Vipotnik stays at Swansea 'for the moment'

'I'd want £30m for him' - Blake on Vipotnik

There have also been the question marks over Vipotnik's future.

There was the school of thought that Swansea might want to cash in on the high value of a player who out-performed his expected goals (xG) by some way last season.

In other words, he scored more goals than the chances suggested he had a right to.

The signing of Ross Stewart following the Scotland forward's departure from Southampton only added weight to that theory.

But the only concrete bid was turned down, Hull City's £10m offer knocked back, while Matos claimed he was not aware of deadline-day interest from Burnley.

The Portuguese did concede that with transfer windows still open elsewhere – most notably in Saudi Arabia – a departure cannot be ruled out.

Former Wales striker Nathan Blake, who valued Vipotnik at around £25m, said the speculation and shift to the bench will have hit Vipotnik, claiming late last month: "I could see by looking at his face, he's not on it. He's probably two or three yards short mentally because of what is going on."

Last week Matos conceded it might have had an impact, saying: "It's normal that some things can unsettle you when we are in the middle of all of this."

With Stewart injured for Tuesday's game against his former side, and Swansea likely to rotate personnel as they play a third match in seven days, Matos was asked whether this was the game to reintroduce Vipotnik to the starting line-up.

"We need to see what is best for the team," said Matos, offering a smile but no commitment.

What he did offer, though, was conviction that the player of last season is still there in more ways than one.

"Besides the goals, he contributes a lot for the other parts of the game," said Matos.

"I think [in Saturday's 0-0 draw] against Wrexham he came on really sharp with the right mindset, fought for the duels, fought for the first ball, second ball, tried to arrive in the box for that chance.

"Even with that he was helping building.

"So all that is coming - then it's just a matter of scoring and he will score for sure."

Swansea would welcome that as they look to show their impressive start should be taken seriously.

Their record of conceding just once so far is the meanest in the EFL, although they take on a Saints team who put five past Millwall last time out at St Mary's.

"Southampton I think is one of the best teams on the league, a proper contender to win the league and to get promoted," said Matos. "So it will be a really good game.

"We need to analyse the Wrexham game, see the priorities and then see as well Southampton.

"But I expect a really, really good game for us to compete."
